<h1 id="box-platform-api">Box Platform API v2.0.0</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

[Box Platform](https://box.dev) provides functionality to provide access to content stored within [Box](https://box.com). It provides endpoints for basic manipulation of files and folders, management of users within an enterprise, as well as more complex topics such as legal holds and retention policies.

Base URLs:

* <a href="https://api.box.com/2.0">https://api.box.com/2.0</a> - Box Platform API server

<a href="https://cloud.app.box.com/s/rmwxu64h1ipr41u49w3bbuvbsa29wku9">Terms of service</a>
Email: <a href="mailto:devrel@box.com">Box, Inc</a> 
Web: <a href="https://box.dev">Box, Inc</a> 
License: <a href="http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0">Apache-2.0</a>

<a href="https://developer.box.com">Box Developer Documentation</a>

# Authentication

- oAuth2 authentication.

    - Flow: authorizationCode
    - Authorization URL = [https://account.box.com/api/oauth2/authorize](https://account.box.com/api/oauth2/authorize)
    - Token URL = [https://api.box.com/oauth2/token](https://api.box.com/oauth2/token)

|Scope|Scope Description|
|---|---|
|manage_app_users|Provision and manage app users|
|manage_data_retention|Manage data retention polices|
|manage_enterprise_properties|Manage enterprise properties|
|manage_groups|Manage an enterprise's groups|
|manage_legal_hold|Manage Legal Holds|
|manage_managed_users|Provision and manage managed users|
|manage_webhook|Create webhooks programmatically through the API|
|root_readonly|Read all files and folders stored in Box|
|root_readwrite|Read and write all files and folders stored in Box|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-authorization">Authorization</h1>

## Authorize user

<a id="opIdget_authorize"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=ly1nj6n11vionaie65emwzk575hnnmrk'
```

`GET /authorize`

Authorize a user by sending them through the [Box](https://box.com)
website and request their permission to act on their behalf.

This is the first step when authenticating a user using
OAuth 2.0. To request a user's authorization to use the Box APIs
on their behalf you will need to send a user to the URL with this
format.

<h3 id="authorize-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|response_type|query|string(token)|true|The type of response we'd like to receive.|
|client_id|query|string|true|The Client ID of the application that is requesting to authenticate<br>the user. To get the Client ID for your application, log in to your<br>Box developer console and click the **Edit Application** link for<br>the application you're working with. In the OAuth 2.0 Parameters section<br>of the configuration page, find the item labelled `client_id`. The<br>text of that item is your application's Client ID.|
|redirect_uri|query|string(url)|false|The URI to which Box redirects the browser after the user has granted<br>or denied the application permission. This URI match one of the redirect<br>URIs in the configuration of your application. It must be a<br>valid HTTPS URI and it needs to be able to handle the redirection to<br>complete the next step in the OAuth 2.0 flow.<br>Although this parameter is optional, it must be a part of the<br>authorization URL if you configured multiple redirect URIs<br>for the application in the developer console. A missing parameter causes<br>a `redirect_uri_missing` error after the user grants application access.|
|state|query|string|false|A custom string of your choice. Box will pass the same string to<br>the redirect URL when authentication is complete. This parameter<br>can be used to identify a user on redirect, as well as protect<br>against hijacked sessions and other exploits.|
|scope|query|string|false|A comma-separated list of application scopes you'd like to<br>authenticate the user for. This defaults to all the scopes configured<br>for the application in its configuration page.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|response_type|code|

<h3 id="authorize-user-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Does not return any data, but rather should be used in the browser.|Inline|
|default|Default|Does not return any data, but rather should be used in the browser.|Inline|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Revoke access token

<a id="opIdpost_oauth2_revoke"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/oauth2/revoke \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'client_id=ly1nj6n11vionaie65emwzk575hnnmrk&client_secret=hOzsTeFlT6ko0dme22uGbQal04SBPYc1&token=n22JPxrh18m4Y0wIZPIqYZK7VRrsMTWW'
```

`POST /oauth2/revoke`

Revoke an active Access Token, effectively logging a user out
that has been previously authenticated.

> Body parameter

```yaml
client_id: ly1nj6n11vionaie65emwzk575hnnmrk
client_secret: hOzsTeFlT6ko0dme22uGbQal04SBPYc1
token: n22JPxrh18m4Y0wIZPIqYZK7VRrsMTWW
```

<h3 id="revoke-access-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PostOAuth2Revoke](#schemapostoauth2revoke)|false|none|
|» client_id|body|string|false|The Client ID of the application requesting to revoke the<br>access token.|
|» client_secret|body|string|false|The client secret of the application requesting to revoke<br>an access token.|
|» token|body|string(token)|false|The access token to revoke.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": "invalid_client",
  "error_description": "The client credentials are not valid"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": "invalid_client",
  "error_description": "The client credentials are not valid"
}
```

<h3 id="revoke-access-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns an empty response when the token was successfully revoked.|None|
|400|Bad Request|An authentication error.|[OAuth2Error](#schemaoauth2error)|
|default|Default|An authentication error.|[OAuth2Error](#schemaoauth2error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Request access token

<a id="opIdpost_oauth2_token"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/oauth2/token \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'actor_token=c3FIOG9vSGV4VHo4QzAyg5T1JvNnJoZ3ExaVNyQWw6WjRsanRKZG5lQk9qUE1BVQ&actor_token_type=urn%3Aietf%3Aparams%3Aoauth%3Atoken-type%3Aid_token&assertion=xxxxx.yyyyy.zzzzz&box_shared_link=https%3A%2F%2Fcloud.box.com%2Fs%2F123456&box_subject_id=123456789&box_subject_type=enterprise&client_id=ly1nj6n11vionaie65emwzk575hnnmrk&client_secret=hOzsTeFlT6ko0dme22uGbQal04SBPYc1&code=n22JPxrh18m4Y0wIZPIqYZK7VRrsMTWW&grant_type=authorization_code&refresh_token=c3FIOG9vSGV4VHo4QzAyg5T1JvNnJoZ3ExaVNyQWw6WjRsanRKZG5lQk9qUE1BVQ&resource=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.box.com%2F2.0%2Ffiles%2F123456&scope=item_upload%20item_preview%20base_explorer&subject_token=c3FIOG9vSGV4VHo4QzAyg5T1JvNnJoZ3ExaVNyQWw6WjRsanRKZG5lQk9qUE1BVQ&subject_token_type=urn%3Aietf%3Aparams%3Aoauth%3Atoken-type%3Aaccess_token'
```

`POST /oauth2/token`

Request an Access Token using either a client-side obtained OAuth 2.0
authorization code or a server-side JWT assertion.

An Access Token is a string that enables Box to verify that a
request belongs to an authorized session. In the normal order of
operations you will begin by requesting authentication from the
[authorize](#get-authorize) endpoint and Box will send you an
authorization code.

You will then send this code to this endpoint to exchange it for
an Access Token. The returned Access Token can then be used to to make
Box API calls.

> Body parameter

```yaml
actor_token: c3FIOG9vSGV4VHo4QzAyg5T1JvNnJoZ3ExaVNyQWw6WjRsanRKZG5lQk9qUE1BVQ
actor_token_type: "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token"
assertion: xxxxx.yyyyy.zzzzz
box_shared_link: "https://cloud.box.com/s/123456"
box_subject_id: "123456789"
box_subject_type: enterprise
client_id: ly1nj6n11vionaie65emwzk575hnnmrk
client_secret: hOzsTeFlT6ko0dme22uGbQal04SBPYc1
code: n22JPxrh18m4Y0wIZPIqYZK7VRrsMTWW
grant_type: authorization_code
refresh_token: c3FIOG9vSGV4VHo4QzAyg5T1JvNnJoZ3ExaVNyQWw6WjRsanRKZG5lQk9qUE1BVQ
resource: "https://api.box.com/2.0/files/123456"
scope: item_upload item_preview base_explorer
subject_token: c3FIOG9vSGV4VHo4QzAyg5T1JvNnJoZ3ExaVNyQWw6WjRsanRKZG5lQk9qUE1BVQ
subject_token_type: "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token"
```

<h3 id="request-access-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PostOAuth2Token](#schemapostoauth2token)|false|none|
|» actor_token|body|string(token)|false|The token used to create an annotator token.<br>This is a JWT assertion.<br><br>Used in combination with `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`<br>as the `grant_type`.|
|» actor_token_type|body|string(urn)|false|The type of `actor_token` passed in.<br><br>Used in combination with `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`<br>as the `grant_type`.|
|» assertion|body|string(jwt)|false|A JWT assertion for which to request a new access token.<br><br>Used in combination with `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer`<br>as the `grant_type`.|
|» box_shared_link|body|string(url)|false|Full URL of the shared link on the file or folder<br>that the token should be generated for.|
|» box_subject_id|body|string|false|Used in combination with `client_credentials` as the `grant_type`.<br>Value is determined by `box_subject_type`. If `user` use user ID and if<br>`enterprise` use enterprise ID.|
|» box_subject_type|body|string|false|Used in combination with `client_credentials` as the `grant_type`.|
|» client_id|body|string|false|The Client ID of the application requesting an access token.<br><br>Used in combination with `authorization_code`, `client_credentials`, or<br>`urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer` as the `grant_type`.|
|» client_secret|body|string|false|The client secret of the application requesting an access token.<br><br>Used in combination with `authorization_code`, `client_credentials`, or<br>`urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer` as the `grant_type`.|
|» code|body|string(token)|false|The client-side authorization code passed to your application by<br>Box in the browser redirect after the user has successfully<br>granted your application permission to make API calls on their<br>behalf.<br><br>Used in combination with `authorization_code` as the `grant_type`.|
|» grant_type|body|string(urn)|true|The type of request being made, either using a client-side obtained<br>authorization code, a refresh token, a JWT assertion, client credentials<br>grant or another access token for the purpose of downscoping a token.|
|» refresh_token|body|string(token)|false|A refresh token used to get a new access token with.<br><br>Used in combination with `refresh_token` as the `grant_type`.|
|» resource|body|string(url)|false|Full URL for the file that the token should be generated for.|
|» scope|body|string(space_delimited_list)|false|The space-delimited list of scopes that you want apply to the<br>new access token.<br><br>The `subject_token` will need to have all of these scopes or<br>the call will error with **401 Unauthorized**.|
|» subject_token|body|string(token)|false|The token to exchange for a downscoped token. This can be a regular<br>access token, a JWT assertion, or an app token.<br><br>Used in combination with `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`<br>as the `grant_type`.|
|» subject_token_type|body|string|false|The type of `subject_token` passed in.<br><br>Used in combination with `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange`<br>as the `grant_type`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» actor_token_type|urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token|
|» box_subject_type|enterprise|
|» box_subject_type|user|
|» grant_type|authorization_code|
|» grant_type|refresh_token|
|» grant_type|client_credentials|
|» grant_type|urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer|
|» grant_type|urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange|
|» subject_token_type|urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "access_token": "c3FIOG9vSGV4VHo4QzAyg5T1JvNnJoZ3ExaVNyQWw6WjRsanRKZG5lQk9qUE1BVQ",
  "expires_in": 3600,
  "issued_token_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token",
  "refresh_token": "c3FIOG9vSGV4VHo4QzAyg5T1JvNnJoZ3ExaVNyQWw6WjRsanRKZG5lQk9qUE1BVQ",
  "restricted_to": [
    {
      "object": {
        "etag": "1",
        "id": "12345",
        "type": "file",
        "file_version": {
          "id": "12345",
          "type": "file_version",
          "sha1": "134b65991ed521fcfe4724b7d814ab8ded5185dc"
        },
        "name": "Contract.pdf",
        "sequence_id": {},
        "sha1": "85136C79CBF9FE36BB9D05D0639C70C265C18D37"
      },
      "scope": "item_download"
    }
  ],
  "token_type": "bearer"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": "invalid_client",
  "error_description": "The client credentials are not valid"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": "invalid_client",
  "error_description": "The client credentials are not valid"
}
```

<h3 id="request-access-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a new Access Token that can be used to make authenticated<br>API calls by passing along the token in a authorization header as<br>follows `Authorization: Bearer <Token>`.|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|
|400|Bad Request|An authentication error.|[OAuth2Error](#schemaoauth2error)|
|default|Default|An authentication error.|[OAuth2Error](#schemaoauth2error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Refresh access token

<a id="opIdpost_oauth2_token#refresh"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/oauth2/token#refresh' \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d 'client_id=ly1nj6n11vionaie65emwzk575hnnmrk&client_secret=hOzsTeFlT6ko0dme22uGbQal04SBPYc1&grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=c3FIOG9vSGV4VHo4QzAyg5T1JvNnJoZ3ExaVNyQWw6WjRsanRKZG5lQk9qUE1BVQ'
```

`POST /oauth2/token#refresh`

Refresh an Access Token using its client ID, secret, and refresh token.

> Body parameter

```yaml
client_id: ly1nj6n11vionaie65emwzk575hnnmrk
client_secret: hOzsTeFlT6ko0dme22uGbQal04SBPYc1
grant_type: refresh_token
refresh_token: c3FIOG9vSGV4VHo4QzAyg5T1JvNnJoZ3ExaVNyQWw6WjRsanRKZG5lQk9qUE1BVQ
```

<h3 id="refresh-access-token-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[PostOAuth2Token--RefreshAccessToken](#schemapostoauth2token--refreshaccesstoken)|false|none|
|» client_id|body|string|true|The client ID of the application requesting to refresh the token.|
|» client_secret|body|string|true|The client secret of the application requesting to refresh the token.|
|» grant_type|body|string(urn)|true|The type of request being made, in this case a refresh request.|
|» refresh_token|body|string(token)|true|The refresh token to refresh.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» grant_type|refresh_token|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "access_token": "c3FIOG9vSGV4VHo4QzAyg5T1JvNnJoZ3ExaVNyQWw6WjRsanRKZG5lQk9qUE1BVQ",
  "expires_in": 3600,
  "issued_token_type": "urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token",
  "refresh_token": "c3FIOG9vSGV4VHo4QzAyg5T1JvNnJoZ3ExaVNyQWw6WjRsanRKZG5lQk9qUE1BVQ",
  "restricted_to": [
    {
      "object": {
        "etag": "1",
        "id": "12345",
        "type": "file",
        "file_version": {
          "id": "12345",
          "type": "file_version",
          "sha1": "134b65991ed521fcfe4724b7d814ab8ded5185dc"
        },
        "name": "Contract.pdf",
        "sequence_id": {},
        "sha1": "85136C79CBF9FE36BB9D05D0639C70C265C18D37"
      },
      "scope": "item_download"
    }
  ],
  "token_type": "bearer"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "error": "invalid_client",
  "error_description": "The client credentials are not valid"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": "invalid_client",
  "error_description": "The client credentials are not valid"
}
```

<h3 id="refresh-access-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a new Access Token that can be used to make authenticated<br>API calls by passing along the token in a authorization header as<br>follows `Authorization: Bearer <Token>`.|[AccessToken](#schemaaccesstoken)|
|400|Bad Request|An authentication error.|[OAuth2Error](#schemaoauth2error)|
|default|Default|An authentication error.|[OAuth2Error](#schemaoauth2error)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h1 id="box-platform-api-box-sign">Box Sign</h1>

## List sign requests

<a id="opIdget_sign_requests"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sign_requests \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /sign_requests`

Gets sign requests created by a user. If the `sign_files` and/or
`parent_folder` are deleted, the sign request will not return in the list.

<h3 id="list-sign-requests-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

## Create sign request

<a id="opIdpost_sign_requests"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/sign_requests \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "are_reminders_enabled": true,
```

`POST /sign_requests`

Creates a sign request. This involves preparing a document for signing and
sending the sign request to signers.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "are_reminders_enabled": true,
  "are_text_signatures_enabled": true,
  "days_valid": 2,
  "declined_redirect_url": "https://declined-redirect.com",
  "email_message": "Hello! Please sign the document below",
  "email_subject": "Sign Request from Acme",
  "external_id": "123",
  "is_document_preparation_needed": true,
  "is_phone_verification_required_to_view": true,
  "name": "name",
  "parent_folder": {
    "etag": "1",
    "id": "12345",
    "type": "folder",
    "name": "Contracts",
    "sequence_id": {}
  },
  "prefill_tags": [
    {
      "checkbox_value": true,
      "date_value": "2021-04-26T08:12:13.982Z",
      "document_tag_id": "1234",
      "text_value": "text"
    }
  ],
  "redirect_url": "https://www.example.com",
  "signature_color": "blue",
  "signers": [
    {
      "declined_redirect_url": "https://declined-example.com",
      "email": "example@gmail.com",
      "embed_url_external_user_id": "1234",
      "is_in_person": true,
      "login_required": true,
      "order": 2,
      "password": "SecretPassword123",
      "redirect_url": "https://example.com",
      "role": "signer",
      "verification_phone_number": "6314578901"
    }
  ],
  "source_files": [
    {
      "etag": "1",
      "id": "12345",
      "type": "file",
      "file_version": {
        "id": "12345",
        "type": "file_version",
        "sha1": "134b65991ed521fcfe4724b7d814ab8ded5185dc"
      },
      "name": "Contract.pdf",
      "sequence_id": {},
      "sha1": "85136C79CBF9FE36BB9D05D0639C70C265C18D37"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-sign-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[SignRequestCreateRequest](#schemasignrequestcreaterequest)|false|none|
|» are_reminders_enabled|body|boolean|false|Reminds signers to sign a document on day 3, 8, 13 and 18. Reminders are only sent to outstanding signers.|
|» are_text_signatures_enabled|body|boolean|false|Disables the usage of signatures generated by typing (text).|
|» days_valid|body|integer \| null|false|Number of days after which this request will automatically expire if not completed.|
|» declined_redirect_url|body|string \| null|false|The uri that a signer will be redirected to after declining to sign a document.|
|» email_message|body|string \| null|false|Message to include in sign request email. The field is cleaned through sanitization of specific characters. However, some html tags are allowed. Links included in the message are also converted to hyperlinks in the email. The message may contain the following html tags including `a`, `abbr`, `acronym`, `b`, `blockquote`, `code`, `em`, `i`, `ul`, `li`, `ol`, and `strong`. Be aware that when the text to html ratio is too high, the email may end up in spam filters. Custom styles on these tags are not allowed. If this field is not passed, a default message will be used.|
|» email_subject|body|string \| null|false|Subject of sign request email. This is cleaned by sign request. If this field is not passed, a default subject will be used.|
|» external_id|body|string \| null|false|This can be used to reference an ID in an external system that the sign request is related to.|
|» is_document_preparation_needed|body|boolean|false|Indicates if the sender should receive a `prepare_url` in the response to complete document preparation via UI.|
|» is_phone_verification_required_to_view|body|boolean \| null|false|Forces signers to verify a text message prior to viewing the document. You must specify the phone number of signers to have this setting apply to them.|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the sign request.|
|» parent_folder|body|object|true|none|
|» » etag|body|string \| null|false|The HTTP `etag` of this folder. This can be used within some API<br>endpoints in the `If-Match` and `If-None-Match` headers to only<br>perform changes on the folder if (no) changes have happened.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting a folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folders/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.|
|» » type|body|string|true|`folder`|
|» » name|body|string|false|The name of the folder.|
|» » sequence_id|body|object|false|none|
|» prefill_tags|body|[[SignRequestPrefillTag](#schemasignrequestprefilltag)]|false|When a document contains sign related tags in the content, you can prefill them using this `prefill_tags` by referencing the 'id' of the tag as the `external_id` field of the prefill tag.|
|» redirect_url|body|string \| null|false|When specified, signature request will be redirected to this url when a document is signed.|
|» signature_color|body|string \| null|false|Force a specific signature color (blue, black, or red).|
|» signers|body|[[SignRequestCreateSigner](#schemasignrequestcreatesigner)]|true|Array of signers for the sign request. 35 is the<br>max number of signers permitted.|
|» source_files|body|[[File--Mini](#schemafile--mini)]|true|List of files to create a signing document from. This is currently<br>limited to 10 files. Only the ID and type fields are required<br>for each file. The array will be empty if the `source_files`<br>are deleted.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|folder|
|» signature_color|blue|
|» signature_color|black|
|» signature_color|red|

`POST /metadata_templates/schema#classifications`

When an enterprise does not yet have any classifications, this API call
initializes the classification template with an initial set of
classifications.

If an enterprise already has a classification, the template will already
exist and instead an API call should be made to add additional
classifications.

The classification can only be updated if a classification has already been
applied to the folder before. When editing classifications, only values are
defined for the enterprise will be accepted.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "op": "replace",
    "path": "/Box__Security__Classification__Key",
    "value": "Sensitive"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="update-classification-on-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|body|body|[object]|false|none|
|» op|body|string|false|`replace`|
|» path|body|string|false|`/Box__Security__Classification__Key`|
|» value|body|string|false|The name of the classification to apply to this folder.<br><br>To list the available classifications in an enterprise,<br>use the classification API to retrieve the<br>[classification template](e://get_metadata_templates_enterprise_securityClassification-6VMVochwUWo_schema)<br>which lists all available classification keys.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» op|replace|
|» path|/Box__Security__Classification__Key|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-collaborations">Collaborations</h1>

## Create collaboration

<a id="opIdpost_collaborations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/collaborations \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "accessible_by": {
      "id": "23522323",
      "login": "john@example.com",
      "type": "user"
    },
    "can_view_path": true,
    "expires_at": "2019-08-29T23:59:00-07:00",
    "item": {
      "id": "11446498",
      "type": "file"
    },
    "role": "editor"
  }'
```

`POST /collaborations`

Adds a collaboration for a single user or a single group to a file
or folder.

Collaborations can be created using email address, user IDs, or a
group IDs.

If a collaboration is being created with a group, access to
this endpoint is dependent on the group's ability to be invited.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "accessible_by": {
    "id": "23522323",
    "login": "john@example.com",
    "type": "user"
  },
  "can_view_path": true,
  "expires_at": "2019-08-29T23:59:00-07:00",
  "item": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "file"
  },
  "role": "editor"
}
```

<h3 id="create-collaboration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|notify|query|boolean|false|Determines if users should receive email notification<br>for the action performed.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» accessible_by|body|object|true|The user or group to give access to the item.|
|» » id|body|string|false|The ID of the user or group.<br><br>Alternatively, use `login` to specify a user by email<br>address.|
|» » login|body|string|false|The email address of the user to grant access to the item.<br><br>Alternatively, use `id` to specify a user by user ID.|
|» » type|body|string|true|The type of collaborator to invite.|
|» can_view_path|body|boolean|false|Determines if the invited users can see the entire parent path to<br>the associated folder. The user will not gain privileges in any<br>parent folder and therefore can not see content the user is not<br>collaborated on.<br><br>Be aware that this meaningfully increases the time required to load the<br>invitee's **All Files** page. We recommend you limit the number of<br>collaborations with `can_view_path` enabled to 1,000 per user.<br><br>Only owner or co-owners can invite collaborators with a `can_view_path` of<br>`true`.<br><br>`can_view_path` can only be used for folder collaborations.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time)|false|Set the expiration date for the collaboration. At this date, the<br>collaboration will be automatically removed from the item.<br><br>This feature will only work if the **Automatically remove invited<br>collaborators: Allow folder owners to extend the expiry date**<br>setting has been enabled in the **Enterprise Settings**<br>of the **Admin Console**. When the setting is not enabled,<br>collaborations can not have an expiry date and a value for this<br>field will be result in an error.|
|» item|body|object|true|The item to attach the comment to.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the item that will be granted access to|
|» » type|body|string|true|The type of the item that this collaboration will be<br>granted access to|
|» role|body|string|true|The level of access granted.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|user|
|» » type|group|
|» » type|file|
|» » type|folder|
|» role|editor|
|» role|viewer|
|» role|previewer|
|» role|uploader|
|» role|previewer uploader|
|» role|viewer uploader|
|» role|co-owner|

## Update collaboration

<a id="opIdput_collaborations_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/collaborations/1234 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "can_view_path": true,
    "expires_at": "2019-08-29T23:59:00-07:00",
    "role": "editor",
    "status": "accepted"
  }'
```

`PUT /collaborations/{collaboration_id}`

Updates a collaboration.
Can be used to change the owner of an item, or to
accept collaboration invites.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "can_view_path": true,
  "expires_at": "2019-08-29T23:59:00-07:00",
  "role": "editor",
  "status": "accepted"
}
```

<h3 id="update-collaboration-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|collaboration_id|path|string|true|The ID of the collaboration|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» can_view_path|body|boolean|false|Determines if the invited users can see the entire parent path to<br>the associated folder. The user will not gain privileges in any<br>parent folder and therefore can not see content the user is not<br>collaborated on.<br><br>Be aware that this meaningfully increases the time required to load the<br>invitee's **All Files** page. We recommend you limit the number of<br>collaborations with `can_view_path` enabled to 1,000 per user.<br><br>Only owner or co-owners can invite collaborators with a `can_view_path` of<br>`true`.<br><br>`can_view_path` can only be used for folder collaborations.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time)|false|Update the expiration date for the collaboration. At this date,<br>the collaboration will be automatically removed from the item.<br><br>This feature will only work if the **Automatically remove invited<br>collaborators: Allow folder owners to extend the expiry date**<br>setting has been enabled in the **Enterprise Settings**<br>of the **Admin Console**. When the setting is not enabled,<br>collaborations can not have an expiry date and a value for this<br>field will be result in an error.<br><br>Additionally, a collaboration can only be given an<br>expiration if it was created after the **Automatically remove<br>invited collaborator** setting was enabled.|
|» role|body|string|true|The level of access granted.|
|» status|body|string|false|<!--alex ignore reject--><br>Set the status of a `pending` collaboration invitation,<br>effectively accepting, or rejecting the invite.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» role|editor|
|» role|viewer|
|» role|previewer|
|» role|uploader|
|» role|previewer uploader|
|» role|viewer uploader|
|» role|co-owner|
|» role|owner|
|» status|pending|
|» status|accepted|
|» status|rejected|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns an updated collaboration object unless the owner has changed.|[Collaboration](#schemacollaboration)|
|204|No Content|If the role is changed to `owner`, the collaboration is deleted<br>and a new collaboration is created. The previous `owner` of<br>the old collaboration will be a `co-owner` on the new collaboration.|[Collaboration](#schemacollaboration)|
|403|Forbidden|Returns an error if the authenticated user does not have the right<br>permissions to update the collaboration.<br><br>Additionally, this error may occur when attempting to update the<br>`expires_at` field for the collaboration without the **Automatically<br>remove invited collaborators: Allow folder owners to extend the expiry<br>date** setting enabled in the admin dashboard of the enterprise.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Remove collaboration

`DELETE /collaborations/{collaboration_id}`

## List pending collaborations

<a id="opIdget_collaborations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/collaborations?status=pending' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /collaborations`

Retrieves all pending collaboration invites for this user.

<h3 id="list-pending-collaborations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|status|query|string|true|The status of the collaborations to retrieve|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Queries with offset parameter value<br>exceeding 10000 will be rejected<br>with a 400 response.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|status|pending|

## List file collaborations

<a id="opIdget_files_id_collaborations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/files/12345/collaborations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /files/{file_id}/collaborations`

Retrieves a list of pending and active collaborations for a
file. This returns all the users that have access to the file
or have been invited to the file.

<h3 id="list-file-collaborations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|

## List group collaborations

<a id="opIdget_groups_id_collaborations"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/groups/57645/collaborations \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /groups/{group_id}/collaborations`

Retrieves all the collaborations for a group. The user
must have admin permissions to inspect enterprise's groups.

Each collaboration object has details on which files or
folders the group has access to and with what role.

<h3 id="list-group-collaborations-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|group_id|path|string|true|The ID of the group.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Queries with offset parameter value<br>exceeding 10000 will be rejected<br>with a 400 response.|

## List all collections

<a id="opIdget_collections"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/collections \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /collections`

Retrieves all collections for a given user.

Currently, only the `favorites` collection
is supported.

<h3 id="list-all-collections-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Queries with offset parameter value<br>exceeding 10000 will be rejected<br>with a 400 response.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "limit": 1000,
  "offset": 2000,
  "order": [
    {
      "by": "type",
      "direction": "ASC"
    }
  ],
  "total_count": 5000,
  "entries": [
    {
      "collection_type": "favorites",
      "id": "11446498",
      "name": "Favorites",
      "type": "collection"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h1 id="box-platform-api-comments">Comments</h1>

## Create comment

<a id="opIdpost_comments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/comments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "item": {
      "id": "11446498",
      "type": "file"
    },
    "message": "Review completed!",
    "tagged_message": "@[1234:John] Review completed!"
  }'
```

`POST /comments`

Adds a comment by the user to a specific file, or
as a reply to an other comment.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "item": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "file"
  },
  "message": "Review completed!",
  "tagged_message": "@[1234:John] Review completed!"
}
```

<h3 id="create-comment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» item|body|object|false|The item to attach the comment to.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the item|
|» » type|body|string|true|The type of the item that this comment will be placed on.|
|» message|body|string|true|The text of the comment.<br><br>To mention a user, use the `tagged_message`<br>parameter instead.|
|» tagged_message|body|string|false|The text of the comment, including `@[user_id:name]`<br>somewhere in the message to mention another user, which<br>will send them an email notification, letting them know<br>they have been mentioned.<br><br>The `user_id` is the target user's ID, where the `name`<br>can be any custom phrase. In the Box UI this name will<br>link to the user's profile.<br><br>If you are not mentioning another user, use `message`<br>instead.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|file|
|» » type|comment|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "11446498",
  "type": "comment",
  "created_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "created_by": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "user",
    "login": "ceo@example.com",
    "name": "Aaron Levie"
  },
  "is_reply_comment": true,
  "item": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "file"
  },
  "message": "@Aaron Levie these tigers are cool!",
  "modified_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong."
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456",
  "status": 400,
  "type": "error"
}
```

<h3 id="create-comment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returns the newly created comment object.<br><br>Not all available fields are returned by default. Use the<br>[fields](#param-fields) query parameter to explicitly request<br>any specific fields.|[Comment](#schemacomment)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Queries with offset parameter value<br>exceeding 10000 will be rejected<br>with a 400 response.|

## List enterprise device pins

<a id="opIdget_enterprises_id_device_pinners"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.com/enterprises/3442311/device_pinners \

```

`GET /enterprises/{enterprise_id}/device_pinners`

Retrieves all the device pins within an enterprise.

The user must have admin privileges, and the application
needs the "manage enterprise" scope to make this call.

<h3 id="list-enterprise-device-pins-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enterprise_id|path|string|true|The ID of the enterprise|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort results in. This can be either in alphabetical ascending<br>(`ASC`) or descending (`DESC`) order.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|direction|ASC|
|direction|DESC|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "id": "11446498",
      "owned_by": {
        "id": "11446498",
        "type": "user",
        "login": "ceo@example.com",
        "name": "Aaron Levie"
      },
      "product_name": "iPad",
      "type": "device_pinner"
    }
  ],
  "limit": 200,
  "next_marker": 3000,
  "order": [
    {
      "by": "id",
      "direction": "asc"
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong."
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456",
  "status": 400,

}
```

<h1 id="box-platform-api-downloads">Downloads</h1>

## Download file

<a id="opIdget_files_id_content"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/files/12345/content \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /files/{file_id}/content`

Returns the contents of a file in binary format.

<h3 id="download-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|range|header|string|false|The byte range of the content to download.<br><br>The format `bytes={start_byte}-{end_byte}` can be used to specify<br>what section of the file to download.|
|boxapi|header|string|false|The URL, and optional password, for the shared link of this item.<br><br>This header can be used to access items that have not been<br>explicitly shared with a user.<br><br>Use the format `shared_link=[link]` or if a password is required then<br>use `shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]`.<br><br>This header can be used on the file or folder shared, as well as on any files<br>or folders nested within the item.|
|version|query|string|false|The file version to download|
|access_token|query|string|false|An optional access token that can be used to pre-authenticate this request, which means that a download link can be shared with a browser or a third party service without them needing to know how to handle the authentication.<br>When using this parameter, please make sure that the access token is sufficiently scoped down to only allow read access to that file and no other files or folders.|

> Example responses

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong."
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456",
  "status": 400,
  "type": "error"
}
```

<h3 id="download-file-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|202|Accepted|If the file is not ready to be downloaded yet `Retry-After` header will<br>be returned indicating the time in seconds after which the file will<br>be available for the client to download.<br><br>This response can occur when the file was uploaded immediately before the<br>download request.|None|
|302|Found|If the file is available to be downloaded the response will include a<br>`Location` header for the file on `dl.boxcloud.com`.<br><br>The `dl.boxcloud.com` URL is not persistent and clients will need<br>to follow the redirect in order to actually download the file.|None|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Retry-After|integer||The time in seconds after which to retry the download|
|302|Location|string|url|A pointer to the download URL|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

<h1 id="box-platform-api-events">Events</h1>

## List user and enterprise events

<a id="opIdget_events"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/events \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /events`

Returns up to a year of past events for a given user
or for the entire enterprise.

By default this returns events for the authenticated user. To retrieve events
for the entire enterprise, set the `stream_type` to `admin_logs_streaming`
for live monitoring of new events, or `admin_logs` for querying across
historical events. The user making the API call will
need to have admin privileges, and the application will need to have the
scope `manage enterprise properties` checked.

<h3 id="list-user-and-enterprise-events-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|stream_type|query|string|false|Defines the type of events that are returned<br><br>* `all` returns everything for a user and is the default<br>* `changes` returns events that may cause file tree changes<br>  such as file updates or collaborations.<br>* `sync` is similar to `changes` but only applies to synced folders<br>* `admin_logs` returns all events for an entire enterprise and<br>  requires the user making the API call to have admin permissions. This<br>  stream type is for programmatically pulling from a 1 year history of<br>  events across all users within the enterprise and within a<br>  `created_after` and `created_before` time frame. The complete history<br>  of events will be returned in chronological order based on the event<br>  time, but latency will be much higher than `admin_logs_streaming`.<br>* `admin_logs_streaming` returns all events for an entire enterprise and<br>  requires the user making the API call to have admin permissions. This<br>  stream type is for polling for recent events across all users within<br>  the enterprise. Latency will be much lower than `admin_logs`, but<br>  events will not be returned in chronological order and may<br>  contain duplicates.|
|stream_position|query|string|false|The location in the event stream to start receiving events from.<br><br>* `now` will return an empty list events and<br>the latest stream position for initialization.<br>* `0` or `null` will return all events.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Limits the number of events returned<br><br>Note: Sometimes, the events less than the limit requested can be returned<br>even when there may be more events remaining. This is primarily done in<br>the case where a number of events have already been retrieved and these<br>retrieved events are returned rather than delaying for an unknown amount<br>of time to see if there are any more results.|
|event_type|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of events to filter by. This can only be used when<br>requesting the events with a `stream_type` of `admin_logs` or<br>`adming_logs_streaming`. For any other `stream_type` this value will be<br>ignored.|
|created_after|query|string(date-time)|false|The lower bound date and time to return events for. This can only be used<br>when requesting the events with a `stream_type` of `admin_logs`. For any<br>other `stream_type` this value will be ignored.|
|created_before|query|string(date-time)|false|The upper bound date and time to return events for. This can only be used<br>when requesting the events with a `stream_type` of `admin_logs`. For any<br>other `stream_type` this value will be ignored.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|stream_type|all|
|stream_type|changes|
|stream_type|sync|
|stream_type|admin_logs|
|stream_type|admin_logs_streaming|
|event_type|ACCESS_GRANTED|
|event_type|ACCESS_REVOKED|
|event_type|ADD_DEVICE_ASSOCIATION|
|event_type|ADD_LOGIN_ACTIVITY_DEVICE|
|event_type|ADMIN_LOGIN|
|event_type|APPLICATION_CREATED|
|event_type|APPLICATION_PUBLIC_KEY_ADDED|
|event_type|APPLICATION_PUBLIC_KEY_DELETED|
|event_type|CHANGE_ADMIN_ROLE|
|event_type|CHANGE_FOLDER_PERMISSION|
|event_type|COLLABORATION_ACCEPT|
|event_type|COLLABORATION_EXPIRATION|
|event_type|COLLABORATION_INVITE|
|event_type|COLLABORATION_REMOVE|
|event_type|COLLABORATION_ROLE_CHANGE|
|event_type|COMMENT_CREATE|
|event_type|COMMENT_DELETE|

|event_type|CONTENT_WORKFLOW_POLICY_ADD|

|event_type|EMAIL_ALIAS_REMOVE|
|event_type|ENTERPRISE_APP_AUTHORIZATION_UPDATE|
|event_type|EXTERNAL_COLLAB_SECURITY_SETTINGS|
|event_type|FAILED_LOGIN|
|event_type|FILE_MARKED_MALICIOUS|

## Get events long poll endpoint

<a id="opIdoptions_events"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/events \
  -X OPTIONS \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`OPTIONS /events`

Returns a list of real-time servers that can be used for long-polling updates
to the [event stream](#get-events).

Long polling is the concept where a HTTP request is kept open until the
server sends a response, then repeating the process over and over to receive
updated responses.

Long polling the event stream can only be used for user events, not for
enterprise events.

To use long polling, first use this endpoint to retrieve a list of long poll
URLs. Next, make a long poll request to any of the provided URLs.

When an event occurs in monitored account a response with the value
`new_change` will be sent. The response contains no other details as
it only serves as a prompt to take further action such as sending a
request to the [events endpoint](#get-events) with the last known
`stream_position`.

After the server sends this response it closes the connection. You must now
repeat the long poll process to begin listening for events again.

If no events occur for a while and the connection times out you will
receive a response with the value `reconnect`. When you receive this response
you’ll make another call to this endpoint to restart the process.

If you receive no events in `retry_timeout` seconds then you will need to
make another request to the real-time server (one of the URLs in the response
for this endpoint). This might be necessary due to network errors.

Finally, if you receive a `max_retries` error when making a request to the
real-time server, you should start over by making a call to this endpoint
first.

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "chunk_size": 1,
  "entries": [
    {
      "max_retries": 10,
      "retry_timeout": 610,
      "ttl": 10,
      "type": "realtime_server",
      "url": "http://2.realtime.services.box.net/subscribe?channel=cc807c9c4869ffb1c81a&stream_type=all"
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong."
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456",
  "status": 400,
  "type": "error"
}
```

|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

## Update file request

<a id="opIdput_file_requests_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/file_requests/123 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Please upload required documents",
    "expires_at": "2020-09-28T10:53:43-08:00",
    "is_description_required": true,
    "is_email_required": true,
    "status": "active",
    "title": "Please upload required documents"
  }'
```

`PUT /file_requests/{file_request_id}`

Updates a file request. This can be used to activate or
deactivate a file request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Please upload required documents",
  "expires_at": "2020-09-28T10:53:43-08:00",
  "is_description_required": true,
  "is_email_required": true,
  "status": "active",
  "title": "Please upload required documents"
}
```

<h3 id="update-file-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_request_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a file request.<br><br>The ID for any file request can be determined<br>by visiting a file request builder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/filerequest/123`<br>the `file_request_id` is `123`.|
|if-match|header|string|false|Ensures this item hasn't recently changed before<br>making changes.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `412 Precondition Failed` if it<br>has changed since.|
|body|body|[FileRequestUpdateRequest](#schemafilerequestupdaterequest)|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|An optional new description for the file request. This can be<br>used to change the description of the file request.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The date after which a file request will no longer accept new<br>submissions.<br><br>After this date, the `status` will automatically be set to<br>`inactive`.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» is_description_required|body|boolean|false|Whether a file request submitter is required to provide<br>a description of the files they are submitting.<br><br>When this setting is set to true, the Box UI will show<br>a description field on the file request form.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» is_email_required|body|boolean|false|Whether a file request submitter is required to provide<br>their email address.<br><br>When this setting is set to true, the Box UI will show<br>an email field on the file request form.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» status|body|string|false|An optional new status of the file request.<br><br>When the status is set to `inactive`, the file request<br>will no longer accept new submissions, and any visitor<br>to the file request URL will receive a `HTTP 404` status<br>code.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» title|body|string|false|An optional new title for the file request. This can be<br>used to change the title of the file request.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|active|
|» status|inactive|

```bash
    "is_description_required": true,
    "is_email_required": true,
    "status": "active",
    "title": "Please upload required documents",
    "folder": {
      "id": "42037322",
      "type": "folder"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /file_requests/{file_request_id}/copy`

Copies an existing file request that is already present on one folder,
and applies it to another folder.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Please upload required documents",
  "expires_at": "2020-09-28T10:53:43-08:00",
  "is_description_required": true,
  "is_email_required": true,
  "status": "active",
  "title": "Please upload required documents",
  "folder": {
    "id": "42037322",
    "type": "folder"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="copy-file-request-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_request_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a file request.<br><br>The ID for any file request can be determined<br>by visiting a file request builder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/filerequest/123`<br>the `file_request_id` is `123`.|
|body|body|[FileRequestCopyRequest](#schemafilerequestcopyrequest)|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|An optional new description for the file request. This can be<br>used to change the description of the file request.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» expires_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The date after which a file request will no longer accept new<br>submissions.<br><br>After this date, the `status` will automatically be set to<br>`inactive`.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» is_description_required|body|boolean|false|Whether a file request submitter is required to provide<br>a description of the files they are submitting.<br><br>When this setting is set to true, the Box UI will show<br>a description field on the file request form.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» is_email_required|body|boolean|false|Whether a file request submitter is required to provide<br>their email address.<br><br>When this setting is set to true, the Box UI will show<br>an email field on the file request form.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» status|body|string|false|An optional new status of the file request.<br><br>When the status is set to `inactive`, the file request<br>will no longer accept new submissions, and any visitor<br>to the file request URL will receive a `HTTP 404` status<br>code.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» title|body|string|false|An optional new title for the file request. This can be<br>used to change the title of the file request.<br><br>This will default to the value on the existing file request.|
|» folder|body|object|true|The folder to associate the new file request to.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the folder to associate the new<br>file request to.|
|» » type|body|string|false|`folder`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|active|
|» status|inactive|
|» » type|folder|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-file-version-legal-holds">File version legal holds</h1>

## List file version legal holds

<a id="opIdget_file_version_legal_holds"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/file_version_legal_holds?policy_id=133870' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /file_version_legal_holds`

Get a list of file versions on legal hold for a legal hold
assignment.

Due to ongoing re-architecture efforts this API might not return all file
versions for this policy ID.

Instead, this API will only return file versions held in the legacy
architecture. Two new endpoints will available to request any file versions
held in the new architecture.

For file versions held in the new architecture, the `GET
/legal_hold_policy_assignments/:id/file_versions_on_hold` API can be used to
return all past file versions available for this policy assignment, and the
`GET /legal_hold_policy_assignments/:id/files_on_hold` API can be used to
return any current (latest) versions of a file under legal hold.

The `GET /legal_hold_policy_assignments?policy_id={id}` API can be used to
find a list of policy assignments for a given policy ID.

Once the re-architecture is completed this API will be deprecated.

<h3 id="list-file-version-legal-holds-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|policy_id|query|string|true|The ID of the legal hold policy to get the file version legal<br>holds for.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-file-version-retentions">File version retentions</h1>

`GET /file_version_retentions`

Retrieves all file version retentions for the given enterprise.

<h3 id="list-file-version-retentions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|file_id|query|string|false|Filters results by files with this ID.|
|file_version_id|query|string|false|Filters results by file versions with this ID.|
|policy_id|query|string|false|Filters results by the retention policy with this ID.|
|disposition_action|query|string|false|Filters results by the retention policy with this disposition<br>action.|
|disposition_before|query|string|false|Filters results by files that will have their disposition<br>come into effect before this date.|
|disposition_after|query|string|false|Filters results by files that will have their disposition<br>come into effect after this date.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|

`GET /files/{file_id}/versions`

Versions are only tracked by Box users with premium accounts. To fetch the ID

|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Queries with offset parameter value<br>exceeding 10000 will be rejected<br>with a 400 response.|

## Promote file version

<a id="opIdpost_files_id_versions_current"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/files/12345/versions/current \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "file_version"
  }'
```

`POST /files/{file_id}/versions/current`

Promote a specific version of a file.

If previous versions exist, this method can be used to
promote one of the older versions to the top of the version history.

This creates a new copy of the old version and puts it at the
top of the versions history. The file will have the exact same contents
as the older version, with the the same hash digest, `etag`, and
name as the original.

Other properties such as comments do not get updated to their
former values.

Don't use this endpoint to restore Box Notes,
as it works with file formats such as PDF, DOC,
PPTX or similar.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "11446498",
  "type": "file_version"
}
```

<h3 id="promote-file-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» id|body|string|false|The file version ID|
|» type|body|string|false|The type to promote|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» type|file_version|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "12345",
  "type": "file_version",
  "sha1": "134b65991ed521fcfe4724b7d814ab8ded5185dc",
  "created_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "modified_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "modified_by": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "user",
    "login": "ceo@example.com",
    "name": "Aaron Levie"
  },
  "name": "tigers.jpeg",
  "purged_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "restored_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "restored_by": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "user",
    "login": "ceo@example.com",
    "name": "Aaron Levie"
  },
  "size": 629644,
  "trashed_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "trashed_by": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "user",
    "login": "ceo@example.com",
    "name": "Aaron Levie"
  },
  "uploader_display_name": {}
}
```


`GET /files/{file_id}`

Retrieves the details about a file.

<h3 id="get-file-information-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.<br><br>Additionally this field can be used to query any metadata<br>applied to the file by specifying the `metadata` field as well<br>as the scope and key of the template to retrieve, for example<br>`?field=metadata.enterprise_12345.contractTemplate`.|
|if-none-match|header|string|false|Ensures an item is only returned if it has changed.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `304 Not Modified` if the item has not<br>changed since.|
|boxapi|header|string|false|The URL, and optional password, for the shared link of this item.<br><br>This header can be used to access items that have not been<br>explicitly shared with a user.<br><br>Use the format `shared_link=[link]` or if a password is required then<br>use `shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]`.<br><br>This header can be used on the file or folder shared, as well as on any files<br>or folders nested within the item.|
|x-rep-hints|header|string \| null|true|A header required to request specific `representations`<br>of a file. Use this in combination with the `fields` query<br>parameter to request a specific file representation.<br><br>The general format for these representations is<br>`X-Rep-Hints: [...]` where `[...]` is one or many<br>hints in the format `[fileType?query]`.<br><br>For example, to request a `png` representation in `32x32`<br>as well as `64x64` pixel dimensions provide the following<br>hints.<br><br>`x-rep-hints: [jpg?dimensions=32x32][jpg?dimensions=64x64]`<br><br>Additionally, a `text` representation is available for all<br>document file types in Box using the `[extracted_text]`<br>representation.<br><br>`x-rep-hints: [extracted_text]`|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "etag": "1",
  "id": "12345",
  "type": "file",
  "file_version": {
    "id": "12345",
    "type": "file_version",
    "sha1": "134b65991ed521fcfe4724b7d814ab8ded5185dc"
  },
  "name": "Contract.pdf",
  "sequence_id": {},
  "sha1": "85136C79CBF9FE36BB9D05D0639C70C265C18D37",
  "content_created_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "content_modified_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
```

## Update file

<a id="opIdput_files_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/files/12345 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "The latest reports. Automatically updated",
    "disposition_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "lock": {
      "access": "lock",
      "expires_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "is_download_prevented": true
    },
    "name": "NewFile.txt",
    "parent": {
      "id": "123"
    },
    "permissions": {
      "can_download": "open"
    },
    "shared_link": {
      "access": "open",
      "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
      "permissions": {
        "can_download": true
      },
      "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
    },
    "tags": [
      "approved"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /files/{file_id}`

Updates a file. This can be used to rename or move a file,
create a shared link, or lock a file.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "The latest reports. Automatically updated",
  "disposition_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "lock": {
    "access": "lock",
    "expires_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "is_download_prevented": true
  },
  "name": "NewFile.txt",
  "parent": {
    "id": "123"
  },
  "permissions": {
    "can_download": "open"
  },
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
    "permissions": {
      "can_download": true
    },
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
  },
  "tags": [
    "approved"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|if-match|header|string|false|Ensures this item hasn't recently changed before<br>making changes.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `412 Precondition Failed` if it<br>has changed since.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|The description for a file. This can be seen in the right-hand sidebar panel<br>when viewing a file in the Box web app. Additionally, this index is used in<br>the search index of the file, allowing users to find the file by the content<br>in the description.|
|» disposition_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The retention expiration timestamp for the given file. This<br>date cannot be shortened once set on a file.|
|» lock|body|object|false|Defines a lock on an item. This prevents the item from being<br>moved, renamed, or otherwise changed by anyone other than the user<br>who created the lock.<br><br>Set this to `null` to remove the lock.|
|» » access|body|string|false|The type of this object.|
|» » expires_at|body|string(date-time)|false|Defines the time at which the lock expires.|
|» » is_download_prevented|body|boolean|false|Defines if the file can be downloaded while it is locked.|
|» name|body|string|false|An optional different name for the file. This can be used to<br>rename the file.|
|» parent|body|object|false|none|
|» » id|body|string|false|The ID of parent item|
|» permissions|body|object|false|Defines who can download a file.|
|» » can_download|body|string|false|Defines who is allowed to download this file. The possible<br>values are either `open` for everyone or `company` for<br>the other members of the user's enterprise.<br><br>This setting overrides the download permissions that are<br>normally part of the `role` of a collaboration. When set to<br>`company`, this essentially removes the download option for<br>external users with `viewer` or `editor` a roles.|
|» shared_link|body|object|false|none|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the folder (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br><br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » permissions|body|object|false|none|
|» » » can_download|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for downloading of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared links.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|The tags for this item. These tags are shown in<br>the Box web app and mobile apps next to an item.<br><br>To add or remove a tag, retrieve the item's current tags,<br>modify them, and then update this field.<br><br>There is a limit of 100 tags per item, and 10,000<br>unique tags per enterprise.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » access|lock|
|» » can_download|open|
|» » can_download|company|
|» » access|open|
|» » access|company|
|» » access|collaborators|
