<h3 id="update-file-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a file object.<br><br>Not all available fields are returned by default. Use the<br>[fields](#param-fields) query parameter to explicitly request<br>any specific fields.|[File](#schemafile)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned when the new retention time > maximum retention length.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|401|Unauthorized|Returned when the access token provided in the `Authorization` header<br>is not recognized or not provided.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned if the user does not have all the permissions to complete the<br>update.<br><br>* `access_denied_insufficient_permissions` returned<br>when the authenticated user does not have access<br>to the destination folder to move the file to.<br>* Returned when retention time is shorter or equal to current retention<br>timestamp.<br>* Returned when a `file_id` that is not under retention is entered.<br>* Returned when a file that is retained but the disposition action is set<br>to `remove_retention`<br>* `forbidden_by_policy` is returned if copying a folder is<br>forbidden due to information barrier restrictions.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the file is not found, or the user does not<br>have access to the file.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|405|Method Not Allowed|Returned if the `file_id` is not in a recognized format.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|412|Precondition Failed|Returns an error when the `If-Match` header does not match<br>the current `etag` value of the file. This indicates that the file<br>has changed since it was last requested.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Delete file

<a id="opIddelete_files_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/files/12345 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /files/{file_id}`

Deletes a file, either permanently or by moving it to
the trash.

The the enterprise settings determine whether the item will
be permanently deleted from Box or moved to the trash.

<h3 id="delete-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|if-match|header|string|false|Ensures this item hasn't recently changed before<br>making changes.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `412 Precondition Failed` if it<br>has changed since.|

## Copy file

<a id="opIdpost_files_id_copy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/files/12345/copy \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "FileCopy.txt",
    "parent": {
      "id": "0"
    },
    "version": "0"
  }'
```

`POST /files/{file_id}/copy`

Creates a copy of a file.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "FileCopy.txt",
  "parent": {
    "id": "0"
  },
  "version": "0"
}
```

<h3 id="copy-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|An optional new name for the copied file.<br><br>There are some restrictions to the file name. Names containing<br>non-printable ASCII characters, forward and backward slashes<br>(`/`, `\`), and protected names like `.` and `..` are<br>automatically sanitized by removing the non-allowed<br>characters.|
|» parent|body|object|true|The destination folder to copy the file to.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of folder to copy the file to.|
|» version|body|string|false|An optional ID of the specific file version to copy.|

<h3 id="copy-file-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returns a new file object representing the copied file.<br><br>Not all available fields are returned by default. Use the<br>[fields](#param-fields) query parameter to explicitly request<br>any specific fields.|[File](#schemafile)|
|304|Not Modified|Returns an empty response when the `If-None-Match` header matches<br>the current `etag` value of the file. This indicates that the file<br>has not changed since it was last requested.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returns an error if some of the parameters are missing or<br>not valid.<br><br>* `bad_request` when a parameter is missing.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returns an error when the user does not have the<br>right permissions to create the copy a file.<br><br>* `forbidden_by_policy`: Returned if copying a file is<br>forbidden due to information barrier restrictions.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error if either the source file or the destination<br>folder could not be found, or the authenticated user does not<br>have access to either.<br><br>* `not_found` when the authenticated user does not have access<br>  to the source file or the destination folder|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|409|Conflict|* `operation_blocked_temporary`: Returned if either of the destination<br>  or source folders is locked due to another move, copy, delete or<br>  restore operation in process.<br><br>  The operation can be retried at a later point.<br><br>* `item_name_in_use` when a folder with the same name already<br>  exists.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

## Get file thumbnail

<a id="opIdget_files_id_thumbnail_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/files/12345/thumbnail.png \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /files/{file_id}/thumbnail.{extension}`

Retrieves a thumbnail, or smaller image representation, of a file.

Sizes of `32x32`,`64x64`, `128x128`, and `256x256` can be returned in
the `.png` format and sizes of `32x32`, `160x160`, and `320x320`
can be returned in the `.jpg` format.

Thumbnails can be generated for the image and video file formats listed
[found on our community site][1].

[1]: https://community.box.com/t5/Migrating-and-Previewing-Content/File-Types-and-Fonts-Supported-in-Box-Content-Preview/ta-p/327

<h3 id="get-file-thumbnail-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|extension|path|string|true|The file format for the thumbnail|
|min_height|query|integer|false|The minimum height of the thumbnail|
|min_width|query|integer|false|The minimum width of the thumbnail|
|max_height|query|integer|false|The maximum height of the thumbnail|
|max_width|query|integer|false|The maximum width of the thumbnail|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|extension|png|
|extension|jpg|

<h3 id="get-file-thumbnail-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|When a thumbnail can be created the thumbnail data will be<br>returned in the body of the response.|Inline|
|202|Accepted|Sometimes generating a thumbnail can take a few seconds. In these<br>situations the API returns a `Location`-header pointing to a<br>placeholder graphic for this file type.<br><br>The placeholder graphic can be used in a user interface until the<br>thumbnail generation has completed. The `Retry-After`-header indicates<br>when to the thumbnail will be ready. At that time, retry this endpoint<br>to retrieve the thumbnail.|None|
|302|Found|Returns an error when Box is not able to create a thumbnail for this<br>file type.<br><br>Instead, a `Location`-header pointing to a placeholder graphic for<br>this file type will be returned.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returns an error if some of the parameters are missing or<br>not valid.<br><br>* `requested_preview_unavailable` - an incorrect dimension was<br>  requested. This will happen if the dimension requested is<br>  larger or smaller than the available file sizes for the thumbnail<br>  format, or when when any of the size constraints contradict<br>  each other.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned when the access token provided in the `Authorization` header<br>is not recognized or not provided.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returned if the file is not found, or the user does not<br>have access to the file, or for additional reasons.<br><br>* `preview_cannot_be_generated` - Box does not support thumbnails<br>  for this type of file|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

### Response Headers

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|202|Location|string|url|A pointer to a placeholder graphic that can be used until the<br>thumbnail has been generated.|
|202|Retry-After|integer|int64|The time in seconds after which the thumbnail will be available.<br><br>Your application  only attempt to get the thumbnail again after<br>this time.|
|302|Location|string|url|A pointer to a placeholder graphic that can be used for this<br>file type.|

## List folder locks

<a id="opIdget_folder_locks"></a>

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/folder_locks?folder_id=12345' \
```

`GET /folder_locks`

Retrieves folder lock details for a given folder.

You must be authenticated as the owner or co-owner of the folder to
use this endpoint.

For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|

## Create folder lock

<a id="opIdpost_folder_locks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/folder_locks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "folder": {
      "id": "1234567890",
      "type": "folder"
    },
    "locked_operations": {
      "delete": true,
      "move": true
    }
  }'
```

`POST /folder_locks`

Creates a folder lock on a folder, preventing it from being moved and/or
deleted.

You must be authenticated as the owner or co-owner of the folder to
use this endpoint.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "folder": {
    "id": "1234567890",
    "type": "folder"
  },
  "locked_operations": {
    "delete": true,
    "move": true
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-folder-lock-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» folder|body|object|true|The folder to apply the lock to.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the folder.|
|» » type|body|string|true|The content type the lock is being applied to. Only `folder`<br>is supported.|
|» locked_operations|body|object|false|The operations to lock for the folder. If `locked_operations` is<br>included in the request, both `move` and `delete` must also be<br>included and both set to `true`.|
|» » delete|body|boolean|true|Whether deleting the folder should be locked.|
|» » move|body|boolean|true|Whether moving the folder should be locked.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "created_at": "2020-09-14T23:12:53Z",
  "created_by": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "user"
  },

    "etag": "1",
    "id": "12345",
    "type": "folder",
    "name": "Contracts",
    "sequence_id": {}
  },
  "id": "12345678",
  "lock_type": "freeze",
  "locked_operations": {
    "delete": true,
    "move": true
  },
  "type": "folder_lock"
}
```

<h1 id="box-platform-api-folders">Folders</h1>

## Create folder

<a id="opIdpost_folders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/folders \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "folder_upload_email": {
      "access": "open"
    },
    "name": "New Folder",
    "parent": {
      "id": "0"
    },
    "sync_state": "synced"
  }'
```

`POST /folders`

Creates a new empty folder within the specified parent folder.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "folder_upload_email": {
    "access": "open"
  },
  "name": "New Folder",
  "parent": {
    "id": "0"
  },
  "sync_state": "synced"
}
```

<h3 id="create-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» folder_upload_email|body|object|false|none|
|» » access|body|string|false|When this parameter has been set, users can email files<br>to the email address that has been automatically<br>created for this folder.<br><br>To create an email address, set this property either when<br>creating or updating the folder.<br><br>When set to `collaborators`, only emails from registered email<br>addresses for collaborators will be accepted. This includes<br>any email aliases a user might have registered.<br><br>When set to `open` it will accept emails from any email<br>address.|
|» name|body|string|true|The name for the new folder.<br><br>There are some restrictions to the file name. Names containing<br>non-printable ASCII characters, forward and backward slashes<br>(`/`, `\`), as well as names with trailing spaces are<br>prohibited.<br><br>Additionally, the names `.` and `..` are<br>not allowed either.|
|» parent|body|object|true|The parent folder to create the new folder within.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of parent folder|
|» sync_state|body|string|false|Specifies whether a folder should be synced to a<br>user's device or not. This is used by Box Sync<br>(discontinued) and is not used by Box Drive.|

#### Enumerated Values

|---|---|
|» » access|open|
|» » access|collaborators|
|» sync_state|synced|
|» sync_state|not_synced|
|» sync_state|partially_synced|

## Get folder information

<a id="opIdget_folders_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/folders/12345 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /folders/{folder_id}`

Retrieves details for a folder, including the first 100 entries
in the folder.

To fetch more items within the folder, please use the
[Get items in a folder](#get-folders-id-items) endpoint.

<h3 id="get-folder-information-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.<br><br>Additionally this field can be used to query any metadata<br>applied to the file by specifying the `metadata` field as well<br>as the scope and key of the template to retrieve, for example<br>`?field=metadata.enterprise_12345.contractTemplate`.|
|if-none-match|header|string|false|Ensures an item is only returned if it has changed.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `304 Not Modified` if the item has not<br>changed since.|
|boxapi|header|string|false|The URL, and optional password, for the shared link of this item.<br><br>This header can be used to access items that have not been<br>explicitly shared with a user.<br><br>Use the format `shared_link=[link]` or if a password is required then<br>use `shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]`.<br><br>This header can be used on the file or folder shared, as well as on any files<br>or folders nested within the item.|

Use the<br>[fields](#param-fields) query parameter to explicitly request<br>any specific fields.|[Folder](#schemafolder)|

## Update folder

<a id="opIdput_folders_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/folders/12345 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "can_non_owners_invite": true,
    "can_non_owners_view_collaborators": true,
    "collections": [
      {
        "id": "11446498",
        "type": "file"
      }
    ],
    "description": "Legal contracts for the new ACME deal",
    "folder_upload_email": {
      "access": "open"
    },
    "is_collaboration_restricted_to_enterprise": true,
    "name": "New Folder",
    "parent": {
      "id": "0"
    },
    "shared_link": {
      "access": "open",
      "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
      "permissions": {
        "can_download": true
      },
      "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
    },
    "sync_state": "synced",
    "tags": [
      "approved"
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /folders/{folder_id}`

Updates a folder. This can be also be used to move the folder,
create shared links, update collaborations, and more.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "can_non_owners_invite": true,
  "can_non_owners_view_collaborators": true,
  "collections": [
    {
      "id": "11446498",
      "type": "file"
    }
  ],
  "description": "Legal contracts for the new ACME deal",
  "folder_upload_email": {
    "access": "open"
  },
  "is_collaboration_restricted_to_enterprise": true,
  "name": "New Folder",
  "parent": {
    "id": "0"
  },
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
    "permissions": {
      "can_download": true
    },
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
  },
  "sync_state": "synced",
  "tags": [
    "approved"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="update-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|if-match|header|string|false|Ensures this item hasn't recently changed before<br>making changes.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `412 Precondition Failed` if it<br>has changed since.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» can_non_owners_invite|body|boolean|false|Specifies if users who are not the owner<br>of the folder can invite new collaborators to the folder.|
|» can_non_owners_view_collaborators|body|boolean|false|Restricts collaborators who are not the owner of<br>this folder from viewing other collaborations on<br>this folder.<br><br>It also restricts non-owners from inviting new<br>collaborators.<br><br>When setting this field to `false`, it is required<br>to also set `can_non_owners_invite_collaborators` to<br>`false` if it has not already been set.|
|» collections|body|[object]|false|An array of collections to make this folder<br>a member of. Currently<br>we only support the `favorites` collection.<br><br>To get the ID for a collection, use the<br>[List all collections][1] endpoint.<br><br>Passing an empty array `[]` or `null` will remove<br>the folder from all collections.<br><br>[1]: ../advanced-files-and-folders/#get-collections|
|» » id|body|string|false|The unique identifier for this object|
|» » type|body|string|false|The type for this object|
|» description|body|string|false|The optional description of this folder|
|» folder_upload_email|body|object|false|none|
|» » access|body|string|false|When this parameter has been set, users can email files<br>to the email address that has been automatically<br>created for this folder.<br><br>To create an email address, set this property either when<br>creating or updating the folder.<br><br>When set to `collaborators`, only emails from registered email<br>addresses for collaborators will be accepted. This includes<br>any email aliases a user might have registered.<br><br>When set to `open` it will accept emails from any email<br>address.|
|» is_collaboration_restricted_to_enterprise|body|boolean|false|Specifies if new invites to this folder are restricted to users<br>within the enterprise. This does not affect existing<br>collaborations.|
|» name|body|string|false|The optional new name for this folder.|
|» parent|body|object|false|The parent folder for this folder. Use this to move<br>the folder or to restore it out of the trash.|
|» » id|body|string|false|The ID of the new parent folder|
|» shared_link|body|object|false|none|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the folder (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br><br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » permissions|body|object|false|none|
|» » » can_download|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for downloading of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared links.|
|» sync_state|body|string|false|Specifies whether a folder should be synced to a<br>user's device or not. This is used by Box Sync<br>(discontinued) and is not used by Box Drive.|
|» tags|body|[string]|false|The tags for this item. These tags are shown in<br>the Box web app and mobile apps next to an item.<br><br>To add or remove a tag, retrieve the item's current tags,<br>modify them, and then update this field.<br><br>There is a limit of 100 tags per item, and 10,000<br>unique tags per enterprise.|

<h3 id="update-folder-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a folder object for the updated folder<br><br>Not all available fields are returned by default. Use the<br>[fields](#param-fields) query parameter to explicitly request<br>any specific fields.<br><br>This call will return synchronously. This holds true even when<br>moving folders with a large a large number of items in all of its<br>descendants. For very large folders, this means the call could<br>take minutes or hours to return.|[Folder](#schemafolder)|
|400|Bad Request|Returns an error if some of the parameters are missing or<br>not valid, or if a folder lock is preventing a move operation.<br><br>* `bad_request` when a parameter is missing or incorrect. This error also<br>  happens when a password is set for a shared link with an access type<br>  of `open`.<br>* `item_name_too_long` when the folder name is too long.<br>* `item_name_invalid` when the folder name contains<br>  non-valid characters.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returns an error if the user does not have the required<br>access to perform the action.<br><br>* `access_denied_insufficient_permissions`: Returned when the<br>  user does not have access to the folder or parent folder, or if the<br>  folder is being moved and a folder lock has been applied to prevent<br>  such operations.<br><br>* `insufficient_scope`: Returned an error if the application<br>  does not have the right scope to update folders. Make sure<br>  your application has been configured to read and write all files<br>  and folders stored in Box.<br><br>* `forbidden`: Returned when the user is not allowed to perform this<br>  action for other users. This can include trying to create a<br>  Shared Link with a `company` access level on a free account.<br><br>* `forbidden_by_policy`: Returned if copying a folder is<br>   forbidden due to information barrier restrictions.<br><br>Returns an error if there are too many actions in the request body.<br><br>* `operation_limit_exceeded`: Returned when the user passes any<br>parameters in addition to the `parent.id` in the request body.<br>The calls to this endpoint have to be split up.<br>The first call needs to include only the `parent.id`,<br>the next call can include other parameters.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error if the folder or parent folder could not be found,<br>or the authenticated user does not have access to either folder.<br><br>* `not_found` when the authenticated user does not have access<br>  to the folder or parent folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|409|Conflict|* `operation_blocked_temporary`: Returned if either of the destination<br>  or source folders is locked due to another move, copy, delete or<br>  restore operation in progress.<br><br>  The operation can be retried at a later point.<br><br>* `item_name_in_use`: Returned if a folder with the name<br>  already exists in the parent folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|412|Precondition Failed|Returns an error when the `If-Match` header does not match<br>the current `etag` value of the folder. This indicates that the<br>folder has changed since it was last requested.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|503|Service Unavailable|Returns an error when the operation takes longer<br>than 60 seconds. The operation will continue after<br>this response has been returned.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Delete folder

<a id="opIddelete_folders_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/folders/12345 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /folders/{folder_id}`

Deletes a folder, either permanently or by moving it to
the trash.

<h3 id="delete-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|if-match|header|string|false|Ensures this item hasn't recently changed before<br>making changes.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `412 Precondition Failed` if it<br>has changed since.|
|recursive|query|boolean|false|Delete a folder that is not empty by recursively deleting the<br>folder and all of its content.|

## Copy folder

<a id="opIdpost_folders_id_copy"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/folders/0/copy \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "New Folder",
    "parent": {
      "id": "0"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /folders/{folder_id}/copy`

Creates a copy of a folder within a destination folder.

The original folder will not be changed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "New Folder",
  "parent": {
    "id": "0"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="copy-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier of the folder to copy.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder with the ID `0` can not be copied.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|An optional new name for the copied folder.<br><br>There are some restrictions to the file name. Names containing<br>non-printable ASCII characters, forward and backward slashes<br>(`/`, `\`), as well as names with trailing spaces are<br>prohibited.<br><br>Additionally, the names `.` and `..` are<br>not allowed either.|
|» parent|body|object|true|The destination folder to copy the folder to.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of parent folder|

<h3 id="copy-folder-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returns a new folder object representing the copied folder.<br><br>Not all available fields are returned by default. Use the<br>[fields](#param-fields) query parameter to explicitly request<br>any specific fields.|[Folder](#schemafolder)|
|304|Not Modified|Returns an empty response when the `If-None-Match` header matches<br>the current `etag` value of the folder. This indicates that the folder<br>has not changed since it was last requested.|None|
|400|Bad Request|Returns an error if some of the parameters are missing or<br>not valid.<br><br>* `bad_request` when a parameter is missing.<br>* `item_name_too_long` when the new folder name is too long.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returns an error when the user does not have the<br>right permissions to copy a folder.<br><br>* `forbidden_by_policy`: Returned if copying a folder is<br>forbidden due to information barrier restrictions.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error if either the source or destination folder<br>could not be found, or the authenticated user does not<br>have access to either folders.<br><br>* `not_found` when the authenticated user does not have access<br>  to the parent folder|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|409|Conflict|Returns an error if a folder by this name already exists<br>in the destination folder, or if the destination folder<br>is locked.<br><br>* `item_name_in_use` when a folder with the same name already<br>  exists.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Returns an error when trying to copy the root folder.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

## List items in folder

<a id="opIdget_folders_id_items"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/folders/12345/items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /folders/{folder_id}/items`

Retrieves a page of items in a folder. These items can be files,
folders, and web links.

To request more information about the folder itself, like its size,
please use the [Get a folder](#get-folders-id) endpoint instead.

<h3 id="list-items-in-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.<br><br>Additionally this field can be used to query any metadata<br>applied to the file by specifying the `metadata` field as well<br>as the scope and key of the template to retrieve, for example<br>`?field=metadata.enterprise_12345.contractTemplate`.|
|usemarker|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether to use marker-based pagination instead of<br>offset-based pagination. Only one pagination method can<br>be used at a time.<br><br>By setting this value to true, the API will return a `marker` field<br>that can be passed as a parameter to this endpoint to get the next<br>page of the response.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Queries with offset parameter value<br>exceeding 10000 will be rejected<br>with a 400 response.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|boxapi|header|string|false|The URL, and optional password, for the shared link of this item.<br><br>This header can be used to access items that have not been<br>explicitly shared with a user.<br><br>Use the format `shared_link=[link]` or if a password is required then<br>use `shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]`.<br><br>This header can be used on the file or folder shared, as well as on any files<br>or folders nested within the item.|
|sort|query|string|false|Defines the **second** attribute by which items<br>are sorted.<br><br>Items are always sorted by their `type` first, with<br>folders listed before files, and files listed<br>before web links.<br><br>This parameter is not supported for marker-based pagination<br>on the root folder (the folder with an ID of `0`).|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort results in. This can be either in alphabetical ascending<br>(`ASC`) or descending (`DESC`) order.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|sort|id|
|sort|name|
|sort|date|
|sort|size|
|direction|ASC|
|direction|DESC|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "limit": 1000,
  "offset": 2000,
  "order": [
    {
      "by": "type",
      "direction": "ASC"
    }
  ],
  "total_count": 5000,
  "entries": [
    {
      "etag": "1",
      "id": "12345",
      "type": "file",
      "file_version": {
        "id": "12345",

      },
```

<h1 id="box-platform-api-group-memberships">Group memberships</h1>

## Add user to group

<a id="opIdpost_group_memberships"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/group_memberships \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "configurable_permissions": {
      "can_run_reports": true
    },
    "group": {
      "id": "4545523"
    },
    "role": "member",
    "user": {
      "id": "1434325"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /group_memberships`

Creates a group membership. Only users with
admin-level permissions will be able to use this API.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "configurable_permissions": {
    "can_run_reports": true
  },
  "group": {
    "id": "4545523"
  },
  "role": "member",
  "user": {
    "id": "1434325"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-user-to-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» configurable_permissions|body|object|false|Custom configuration for the permissions an admin<br>if a group will receive. This option has no effect<br>on members with a role of `member`.<br><br>Setting these permissions overwrites the default<br>access levels of an admin.<br><br>Specifying a value of "null" for this object will disable<br>all configurable permissions. Specifying permissions will set<br>them accordingly, omitted permissions will be enabled by default.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|boolean|false|A key value pair of custom permissions.|
|» group|body|object|true|The group to add the user to.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the group to add the user to|
|» role|body|string|false|The role of the user in the group.|
|» user|body|object|true|The user to add to the group.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the user to add to the group|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» role|member|
|» role|admin|

`POST /groups`

Creates a new group of users in an enterprise. Only users with admin
permissions can create new groups.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "\"Customer Support Group - as imported from Active Directory\"",
  "external_sync_identifier": "AD:123456",
  "invitability_level": "admins_only",
  "member_viewability_level": "admins_only",
  "name": "Customer Support",
  "provenance": "Active Directory"
}
```

<h3 id="create-group-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|A human readable description of the group.|
|» external_sync_identifier|body|string|false|An arbitrary identifier that can be used by<br>external group sync tools to link this Box Group to<br>an external group.<br><br>Example values of this field<br>could be an **Active Directory Object ID** or a **Google<br>Group ID**.<br><br>We recommend you use of this field in<br>order to avoid issues when group names are updated in<br>either Box or external systems.|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-invites">Invites</h1>

## Create user invite

<a id="opIdpost_invites"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/invites \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "actionable_by": {
      "login": "john@example.com"
    },
    "enterprise": {
      "id": "1232234"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /invites`

Invites an existing external user to join an enterprise.

The existing user can not be part of another enterprise and
must already have a Box account. Once invited, the user will receive an
email and are prompted to accept the invitation within the
Box web application.

This method requires the "Manage An Enterprise" scope enabled for
the application, which can be enabled within the developer console.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "actionable_by": {
    "login": "john@example.com"
  },
  "enterprise": {
    "id": "1232234"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-user-invite-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» actionable_by|body|object|true|The user to invite|
|» » login|body|string|false|The login of the invited user|
|» enterprise|body|object|true|The enterprise to invite the user to|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the enterprise|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "actionable_by": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "user",
    "login": "ceo@example.com",
    "name": "Aaron Levie"
  },
  "created_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "id": "11446498",
  "invited_by": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "user",
    "login": "ceo@example.com",
    "name": "Aaron Levie"
  },
  "invited_to": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "name": "Acme Inc.",
    "type": "enterprise"
  },
  "modified_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "status": "pending",
  "type": "invite"
}
```

```json
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong."
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456",
  "status": 400,
  "type": "error"
}
```

<a id="opIdpost_legal_hold_policies"></a>

```bash
curl https://example.com/legal_hold_policies \

    "description": "A custom policy for the sales team",

    "is_ongoing": true,
    "policy_name": "Sales Policy"
  }'
```

`POST /legal_hold_policies`

Create a new legal hold policy.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "A custom policy for the sales team",
  "filter_ended_at": "2012-12-18T10:53:43-08:00",
  "filter_started_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "is_ongoing": true,
  "policy_name": "Sales Policy"
}
```

<h3 id="create-legal-hold-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|A description for the policy.|
|» filter_ended_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The filter end date.<br><br>When this policy is applied using a `custodian` legal<br>hold assignments, it will only apply to file versions<br>created or uploaded inside of the<br>date range. Other assignment types, such as folders and<br>files, will ignore the date filter.<br><br>Required if `is_ongoing` is set to `false`.|
|» filter_started_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The filter start date.<br><br>When this policy is applied using a `custodian` legal<br>hold assignments, it will only apply to file versions<br>created or uploaded inside of the<br>date range. Other assignment types, such as folders and<br>files, will ignore the date filter.<br><br>Required if `is_ongoing` is set to `false`.|
|» is_ongoing|body|boolean|false|Whether new assignments under this policy should<br>continue applying to files even after initialization.<br><br>When this policy is applied using a legal hold assignment,<br>it will continue applying the policy to any new file versions<br>even after it has been applied.<br><br>For example, if a legal hold assignment is placed on a user<br>today, and that user uploads a file tomorrow, that file will<br>get held. This will continue until the policy is retired.<br><br>Required if no filter dates are set.|
|» policy_name|body|string|true|The name of the policy.|

## List previous file versions for legal hold policy assignment

<a id="opIdget_legal_hold_policy_assignments_id_file_versions_on_hold"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/legal_hold_policy_assignments/753465/file_versions_on_hold \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /legal_hold_policy_assignments/{legal_hold_policy_assignment_id}/file_versions_on_hold`

Get a list of previous file versions for a legal hold
assignment.

In some cases you may only need the latest file versions instead. In these
cases, use the `GET  /legal_hold_policy_assignments/:id/files_on_hold` API
instead to return any current (latest) versions of a file for this legal hold
policy assignment.

Due to ongoing re-architecture efforts this API might not return all files
held for this policy ID. Instead, this API will only return past file versions
held in the newly developed architecture. The `GET /file_version_legal_holds`
API can be used to fetch current and past versions of files held within the
legacy architecture.

The `GET /legal_hold_policy_assignments?policy_id={id}` API can be used to
find a list of policy assignments for a given policy ID.

<h3 id="list-previous-file-versions-for-legal-hold-policy-assignment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|legal_hold_policy_assignment_id|path|string|true|The ID of the legal hold policy assignment|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|

`GET /legal_hold_policy_assignments/{legal_hold_policy_assignment_id}/files_on_hold`

assignment.

In some cases you may want to get previous file versions instead. In these
cases, use the `GET  /legal_hold_policy_assignments/:id/file_versions_on_hold`

find a list of policy assignments for a given policy ID.

<h1 id="box-platform-api-metadata-cascade-policies">Metadata cascade policies</h1>

## List metadata cascade policies

<a id="opIdget_metadata_cascade_policies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/metadata_cascade_policies?folder_id=31232' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /metadata_cascade_policies`

Retrieves a list of all the metadata cascade policies
that are applied to a given folder. This can not be used on the root
folder with ID `0`.

<h3 id="list-metadata-cascade-policies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|query|string|true|Specifies which folder to return policies for. This can not be used on the<br>root folder with ID `0`.|
|owner_enterprise_id|query|string|false|The ID of the enterprise ID for which to find metadata<br>cascade policies. If not specified, it defaults to the<br>current enterprise.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Queries with offset parameter value<br>exceeding 10000 will be rejected<br>with a 400 response.|

## Create metadata cascade policy

<a id="opIdpost_metadata_cascade_policies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/metadata_cascade_policies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "folder_id": "1234567",
    "scope": "enterprise",
    "templateKey": "productInfo"
  }'
```

`POST /metadata_cascade_policies`

Creates a new metadata cascade policy that applies a given
metadata template to a given folder and automatically
cascades it down to any files within that folder.

In order for the policy to be applied a metadata instance must first
be applied to the folder the policy is to be applied to.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "folder_id": "1234567",
  "scope": "enterprise",
  "templateKey": "productInfo"
}
```

<h3 id="create-metadata-cascade-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» folder_id|body|string|true|The ID of the folder to apply the policy to. This folder will<br>need to already have an instance of the targeted metadata<br>template applied to it.|
|» scope|body|string|true|The scope of the targeted metadata template. This template will<br>need to already have an instance applied to the targeted folder.|
|» templateKey|body|string|true|The key of the targeted metadata template. This template will<br>need to already have an instance applied to the targeted folder.<br><br>In many cases the template key is automatically derived<br>of its display name, for example `Contract Template` would<br>become `contractTemplate`. In some cases the creator of the<br>template will have provided its own template key.<br><br>Please [list the templates for an enterprise][list], or<br>get all instances on a [file][file] or [folder][folder]<br>to inspect a template's key.<br><br>[list]: e://get-metadata-templates-enterprise<br>[file]: e://get-files-id-metadata<br>[folder]: e://get-folders-id-metadata|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» scope|global|
|» scope|enterprise|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "id": "6fd4ff89-8fc1-42cf-8b29-1890dedd26d7",
  "owner_enterprise": {
    "id": "690678",
    "type": "enterprise"
  },
  "parent": {
    "id": "1234567",
    "type": "folder"
  },
  "scope": "global",
  "templateKey": "productInfo",
  "type": "metadata_cascade_policy"
}
```

## Force-apply metadata cascade policy to folder

<a id="opIdpost_metadata_cascade_policies_id_apply"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/metadata_cascade_policies/6fd4ff89-8fc1-42cf-8b29-1890dedd26d7/apply \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "conflict_resolution": "none"
  }'
```

`POST /metadata_cascade_policies/{metadata_cascade_policy_id}/apply`

Force the metadata on a folder with a metadata cascade policy to be applied to
all of its children. This can be used after creating a new cascade policy to
enforce the metadata to be cascaded down to all existing files within that
folder.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "conflict_resolution": "none"
}
```

<h3 id="force-apply-metadata-cascade-policy-to-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|metadata_cascade_policy_id|path|string|true|The ID of the cascade policy to force-apply.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» conflict_resolution|body|string|true|Describes the desired behavior when dealing with the conflict<br>where a metadata template already has an instance applied<br>to a child.<br><br>* `none` will preserve the existing value on the file<br>* `overwrite` will force-apply the templates values over<br>  any existing values.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» conflict_resolution|none|
|» conflict_resolution|overwrite|

> Example responses

The metadata<br>cascade operation will be performed asynchronously.<br><br>The API call will return directly, before the cascade operation<br>is complete. There is currently no API to check for the status of this<br>operation.|None|

## Update metadata instance on file

<a id="opIdput_files_id_metadata_id_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/files/12345/metadata/global/properties \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json-patch+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "from": "/nextState",
      "op": "add",
      "path": "/currentState",
      "value": "reviewed"
    }
  ]'
```

`PUT /files/{file_id}/metadata/{scope}/{template_key}`

Updates a piece of metadata on a file.

The metadata instance can only be updated if the template has already been
applied to the file before. When editing metadata, only values that match
the metadata template schema will be accepted.

The update is applied atomically. If any errors occur during the
application of the operations, the metadata instance will not be changed.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "from": "/nextState",
    "op": "add",
    "path": "/currentState",
    "value": "reviewed"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="update-metadata-instance-on-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|scope|path|string|true|The scope of the metadata template|
|template_key|path|string|true|The name of the metadata template|
|body|body|[object]|false|none|
|» from|body|string|false|The location in the metadata JSON object to move or copy a value<br>from. Required for `move` or `copy` operations and must be in the<br>format of a [JSON-Pointer](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901).|
|» op|body|string|false|The type of change to perform on the template. Some<br>of these are hazardous as they will change existing templates.|
|» path|body|string|false|The location in the metadata JSON object<br>to apply the changes to, in the format of a<br>[JSON-Pointer](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901).<br><br>The path must always be prefixed with a `/` to represent the root<br>of the template. The characters `~` and `/` are reserved<br>characters and must be escaped in the key.|
|» value|body|string|false|The value to be set or tested.<br><br>Required for `add`, `replace`, and `test` operations. For `add`,<br>if the value exists already the previous value will be overwritten<br>by the new value. For `replace`, the value must exist before<br>replacing.<br><br>For `test`, the existing value at the `path` location must match<br>the specified value.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|scope|global|
|scope|enterprise|

## Create metadata instance on file

```bash
curl https://example.com/files/12345/metadata/global/properties \
```

`POST /files/{file_id}/metadata/{scope}/{template_key}`

Applies an instance of a metadata template to a file.

In most cases only values that are present in the metadata template
will be accepted, except for the `global.properties` template which accepts
any key-value pair.

|scope|path|string|true|The scope of the metadata template|
|template_key|path|string|true|The name of the metadata template|

## Update metadata instance on folder

<a id="opIdput_folders_id_metadata_id_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/folders/12345/metadata/global/properties \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json-patch+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "from": "/nextState",
      "op": "add",
      "path": "/currentState",
      "value": "reviewed"
    }
  ]'
```

`PUT /folders/{folder_id}/metadata/{scope}/{template_key}`

Updates a piece of metadata on a folder.

The metadata instance can only be updated if the template has already been
applied to the folder before. When editing metadata, only values that match
the metadata template schema will be accepted.

The update is applied atomically. If any errors occur during the
application of the operations, the metadata instance will not be changed.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "from": "/nextState",
    "op": "add",
    "path": "/currentState",
    "value": "reviewed"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="update-metadata-instance-on-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|scope|path|string|true|The scope of the metadata template|
|template_key|path|string|true|The name of the metadata template|
|body|body|[object]|false|none|
|» from|body|string|false|The location in the metadata JSON object to move or copy a value<br>from. Required for `move` or `copy` operations and must be in the<br>format of a [JSON-Pointer](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901).|
|» op|body|string|false|The type of change to perform on the template. Some<br>of these are hazardous as they will change existing templates.|
|» path|body|string|false|The location in the metadata JSON object<br>to apply the changes to, in the format of a<br>[JSON-Pointer](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901).<br><br>The path must always be prefixed with a `/` to represent the root<br>of the template. The characters `~` and `/` are reserved<br>characters and must be escaped in the key.|
|» value|body|string|false|The value to be set or tested.<br><br>Required for `add`, `replace`, and `test` operations. For `add`,<br>if the value exists already the previous value will be overwritten<br>by the new value. For `replace`, the value must exist before<br>replacing.<br><br>For `test`, the existing value at the `path` location must match<br>the specified value.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|scope|global|
|scope|enterprise|
|» op|add|
|» op|replace|
|» op|remove|
|» op|test|
|» op|move|
|» op|copy|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "$parent": "folder_59449484661,",
  "$scope": "enterprise_27335",
  "$template": "marketingCollateral",
  "$version": 1
```

## Create metadata template

<a id="opIdpost_metadata_templates_schema"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/metadata_templates/schema \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "copyInstanceOnItemCopy": true,
    "displayName": "Product Info",
    "fields": [
      {
        "description": "The category",
        "displayName": "Category",
        "hidden": true,
        "key": "category",
        "options": [
          {
            "key": "Category 1"
          }
        ],
        "type": "string"
      }
    ],
    "hidden": true,
    "scope": "enterprise",
    "templateKey": "productInfo"
  }'
```

`POST /metadata_templates/schema`

Creates a new metadata template that can be applied to
files and folders.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "copyInstanceOnItemCopy": true,
  "displayName": "Product Info",
  "fields": [
    {
      "description": "The category",
      "displayName": "Category",
      "hidden": true,
      "key": "category",
      "options": [
        {
          "key": "Category 1"
        }
      ],
      "type": "string"
    }
  ],
  "hidden": true,
  "scope": "enterprise",
  "templateKey": "productInfo"
}
```

<h3 id="create-metadata-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» copyInstanceOnItemCopy|body|boolean|false|Whether or not to copy any metadata attached to a file or folder<br>when it is copied. By default, metadata is not copied along with a<br>file or folder when it is copied.|
|» displayName|body|string|true|The display name of the template.|
|» fields|body|[object]|false|An ordered list of template fields which are part of the template.<br>Each field can be a regular text field, date field, number field,<br>as well as a single or multi-select list.|
|» » description|body|string|false|A description of the field. This is not shown to the user.|
|» » displayName|body|string|true|The display name of the field as it is shown to the user in the web and<br>mobile apps.|
|» » hidden|body|boolean|false|Whether this field is hidden in the UI for the user and can only be set<br>through the API instead.|
|» » key|body|string|true|A unique identifier for the field. The identifier must<br>be unique within the template to which it belongs.|
|» » options|body|[object]|false|A list of options for this field. This is used in combination with the<br>`enum` and `multiSelect` field types.|
|» » » key|body|string|true|The text value of the option. This represents both the display name of the<br>option and the internal key used when updating templates.|
|» » type|body|string|true|The type of field. The basic fields are a `string` field for text, a<br>`float` field for numbers, and a `date` fields to present the user with a<br>date-time picker.<br><br>Additionally, metadata templates support an `enum` field for a basic list<br>of items, and ` multiSelect` field for a similar list of items where the<br>user can select more than one value.|
|» hidden|body|boolean|false|Defines if this template is visible in the Box web app UI, or if<br>it is purely intended for usage through the API.|
|» scope|body|string|true|The scope of the metadata template to create. Applications can<br>only create templates for use within the authenticated user's<br>enterprise.<br><br>This value needs to be set to `enterprise`, as `global` scopes can<br>not be created by applications.|
|» templateKey|body|string|false|A unique identifier for the template. This identifier needs to be<br>unique across the enterprise for which the metadata template is<br>being created.<br><br>When not provided, the API will create a unique `templateKey`<br>based on the value of the `displayName`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » type|string|
|» » type|float|
|» » type|date|
|» » type|enum|
|» » type|multiSelect|

> Example responses

> 201 Response

```json
{
  "copyInstanceOnItemCopy": true,
  "displayName": "Product Info",
  "fields": [
    {
      "description": "The category",
      "displayName": "Category",
      "hidden": true,
      "key": "category",
      "options": [
        {
          "key": "Category 1",
          "id": "45dc2849-a4a7-40a9-a751-4a699a589190"
        }
      ],
      "type": "string",
      "id": "822227e0-47a5-921b-88a8-494760b2e6d2"
    }
  ],
  "hidden": true,
  "id": "58063d82-4128-7b43-bba9-92f706befcdf",
  "scope": "enterprise_123456",
  "templateKey": "productInfo",
  "type": "metadata_template"
}
```

```json
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456",
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|The schema representing the metadata template created.|[MetadataTemplate](#schemametadatatemplate)|
|400|Bad Request|Returned if the request parameters or body is not valid.<br><br>* `bad_request` when the body does not contain a valid request. In many<br>cases this response will include extra details on what fields are missing.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returned when the user does not have the permission to create the metadata<br>template. This can happen for a few reasons, most commonly when the user<br>does not have (co-)admin permissions, or the application tries to create a<br>template with the `global` scope.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

## Update metadata template

<a id="opIdput_metadata_templates_id_id_schema"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/metadata_templates/global/properties/schema \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json-patch+json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '[
    {
      "data": {
        "name": "Aaron Levie"
      },
      "enumOptionKey": "option1",
      "enumOptionKeys": [
        "option1",
        "option2",
        "option3"
      ],
      "fieldKey": "category",
      "fieldKeys": [
        "category",
        "name"
      ],
      "multiSelectOptionKey": "option1",
      "multiSelectOptionKeys": [
        "option1",
        "option2",
        "option3"
      ],
      "op": "addEnumOption"
    }
  ]'
```

`PUT /metadata_templates/{scope}/{template_key}/schema`

Updates a metadata template.

The metadata template can only be updated if the template
already exists.

The update is applied atomically. If any errors occur during the
application of the operations, the metadata template will not be changed.

> Body parameter

```json
[
  {
    "data": {
      "name": "Aaron Levie"
    },
    "enumOptionKey": "option1",
    "enumOptionKeys": [
      "option1",
      "option2",
      "option3"
    ],
    "fieldKey": "category",
    "fieldKeys": [
      "category",
      "name"
    ],
    "multiSelectOptionKey": "option1",
    "multiSelectOptionKeys": [
      "option1",
      "option2",
      "option3"
    ],
    "op": "addEnumOption"
  }
]
```

<h3 id="update-metadata-template-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scope|path|string|true|The scope of the metadata template|
|template_key|path|string|true|The name of the metadata template|
|body|body|[object]|false|none|
|» data|body|object|false|The data for the operation. This will vary depending on the<br>operation being performed.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|The value of a custom data entry.|
|» enumOptionKey|body|string|false|For operations that affect a single `enum` option this defines<br>the key of the option that is affected.|
|» enumOptionKeys|body|[string]|false|For operations that affect multiple `enum` options this defines<br>the keys of the options that are affected.|
|» fieldKey|body|string|false|For operations that affect a single field this defines the key of<br>the field that is affected.|
|» fieldKeys|body|[string]|false|For operations that affect multiple fields this defines the keys<br>of the fields that are affected.|
|» multiSelectOptionKey|body|string|false|For operations that affect a single multi select option this<br>defines the key of the option that is affected.|
|» multiSelectOptionKeys|body|[string]|false|For operations that affect multiple multi select options this<br>defines the keys of the options that are affected.|
|» op|body|string|true|The type of change to perform on the template. Some<br>of these are hazardous as they will change existing templates.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|scope|global|
|scope|enterprise|
|» op|editTemplate|
|» op|addField|
|» op|reorderFields|
|» op|addEnumOption|
|» op|reorderEnumOptions|
|» op|reorderMultiSelectOptions|
|» op|addMultiSelectOption|
|» op|editField|
|» op|removeField|
|» op|editEnumOption|
|» op|removeEnumOption|
|» op|editMultiSelectOption|
|» op|removeMultiSelectOption|

> Example responses

```json
    {
      "description": "The category",

      "key": "category",

        {
```

`GET /recent_items`

by a user, either in the last 90 days or up to the last
1000 items accessed.

<h3 id="list-recently-accessed-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

## Create retention policy

<a id="opIdpost_retention_policies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/retention_policies \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "are_owners_notified": true,
    "can_owner_extend_retention": true,
    "custom_notification_recipients": [
      {
        "id": "11446498",
        "type": "user",
        "login": "ceo@example.com",
        "name": "Aaron Levie"
      }
    ],
    "description": "Policy to retain all reports for at least one month",
    "disposition_action": "permanently_delete",
    "policy_name": "Some Policy Name",
    "policy_type": "finite",
    "retention_length": "365",
    "retention_type": "modifiable"
  }'
```

`POST /retention_policies`

Creates a retention policy.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "are_owners_notified": true,
  "can_owner_extend_retention": true,
  "custom_notification_recipients": [
    {
      "id": "11446498",

    }
  ],
```

<h3 id="create-retention-policy-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» are_owners_notified|body|boolean|false|Whether owner and co-owners of a file are notified<br>when the policy nears expiration.|
|» can_owner_extend_retention|body|boolean|false|Whether the owner of a file will be allowed to<br>extend the retention.|
|» custom_notification_recipients|body|[[User--Mini](#schemauser--mini)]|false|A list of users notified when<br>the retention policy duration is about to end.|
|» description|body|string|false|The additional text description of the retention policy.|
|» disposition_action|body|string|true|The disposition action of the retention policy.<br>`permanently_delete` deletes the content<br>retained by the policy permanently.<br>`remove_retention` lifts retention policy<br>from the content, allowing it to be deleted<br>by users once the retention policy has expired.|
|» policy_name|body|string|true|The name for the retention policy|
|» policy_type|body|string|true|The type of the retention policy. A retention<br>policy type can either be `finite`, where a<br>specific amount of time to retain the content is known<br>upfront, or `indefinite`, where the amount of time<br>to retain the content is still unknown.|
|» retention_length|body|string(int32)|false|The length of the retention policy. This value<br>specifies the duration in days that the retention<br>policy will be active for after being assigned to<br>content.  If the policy has a `policy_type` of<br>`indefinite`, the `retention_length` will also be<br>`indefinite`.|
|» retention_type|body|string|false|Specifies the retention type:<br><br>* `modifiable`: You can modify the retention policy. For example,<br>you can add or remove folders, shorten or lengthen<br>the policy duration, or delete the assignment.<br>Use this type if your retention policy<br>is not related to any regulatory purposes.<br><br>* `non-modifiable`: You can modify the retention policy<br>only in a limited way: add a folder, lengthen the duration,<br>retire the policy, change the disposition action<br>or notification settings. You cannot perform other actions,<br>such as deleting the assignment or shortening the<br>policy duration. Use this type to ensure<br>compliance with regulatory retention policies.|

|» can_owner_extend_retention|false|
|» disposition_action|permanently_delete|
|» disposition_action|remove_retention|
|» policy_type|finite|
|» policy_type|indefinite|
|» retention_type|modifiable|
|» retention_type|non-modifiable|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-search">Search</h1>

## Query files/folders by metadata

<a id="opIdpost_metadata_queries_execute_read"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/metadata_queries/execute_read \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "ancestor_folder_id": "0",
    "fields": [
      "extension",
      "created_at",
      "item_status",
      "metadata.enterprise_1234.contracts",
      "metadata.enterprise_1234.regions.location"
    ],
    "from": "enterprise_123456.someTemplate",
    "limit": 50,
    "marker": "AAAAAmVYB1FWec8GH6yWu2nwmanfMh07IyYInaa7DZDYjgO1H4KoLW29vPlLY173OKsci6h6xGh61gG73gnaxoS+o0BbI1/h6le6cikjlupVhASwJ2Cj0tOD9wlnrUMHHw3/ISf+uuACzrOMhN6d5fYrbidPzS6MdhJOejuYlvsg4tcBYzjauP3+VU51p77HFAIuObnJT0ff",
    "order_by": [
      {
        "direction": "asc",
        "field_key": "amount"
      }
    ],
    "query": "value >= :amount",
    "query_params": {
      "amount": "100"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /metadata_queries/execute_read`

Create a search using SQL-like syntax to return items that match specific
metadata.

By default, this endpoint returns only the most basic info about the items for
which the query matches. To get additional fields for each item, including any
of the metadata, use the `fields` attribute in the query.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "ancestor_folder_id": "0",
  "fields": [
    "extension",
    "created_at",
    "item_status",
    "metadata.enterprise_1234.contracts",
    "metadata.enterprise_1234.regions.location"
  ],
  "from": "enterprise_123456.someTemplate",
  "limit": 50,
  "marker": "AAAAAmVYB1FWec8GH6yWu2nwmanfMh07IyYInaa7DZDYjgO1H4KoLW29vPlLY173OKsci6h6xGh61gG73gnaxoS+o0BbI1/h6le6cikjlupVhASwJ2Cj0tOD9wlnrUMHHw3/ISf+uuACzrOMhN6d5fYrbidPzS6MdhJOejuYlvsg4tcBYzjauP3+VU51p77HFAIuObnJT0ff",
  "order_by": [
    {
      "direction": "asc",
      "field_key": "amount"
    }
  ],
  "query": "value >= :amount",
  "query_params": {
    "amount": "100"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="query-filesfolders-by-metadata-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[MetadataQuery](#schemametadataquery)|false|none|
|» ancestor_folder_id|body|string|true|The ID of the folder that you are restricting the query to. A<br>value of zero will return results from all folders you have access<br>to. A non-zero value will only return results found in the folder<br>corresponding to the ID or in any of its subfolders.|
|» fields|body|[string]|false|By default, this endpoint returns only the most basic info about the items for<br>which the query matches. This attribute can be used to specify a list of<br>additional attributes to return for any item, including its metadata.<br><br>This attribute takes a list of item fields, metadata template identifiers,<br>or metadata template field identifiers.<br><br>For example:<br><br>* `created_by` will add the details of the user who created the item to<br>the response.<br>* `metadata.<scope>.<templateKey>` will return the mini-representation<br>of the metadata instance identified by the `scope` and `templateKey`.<br>* `metadata.<scope>.<templateKey>.<field>` will return all the mini-representation<br>of the metadata instance identified by the `scope` and `templateKey` plus<br>the field specified by the `field` name. Multiple fields for the same<br>`scope` and `templateKey` can be defined.|
|» from|body|string|true|Specifies the template used in the query. Must be in the form<br>`scope.templateKey`. Not all templates can be used in this field,<br>most notably the built-in, Box-provided classification templates<br>can not be used in a query.|
|» limit|body|integer|false|A value between 0 and 100 that indicates the maximum number of results<br>to return for a single request. This only specifies a maximum<br>boundary and will not guarantee the minimum number of results<br>returned.|
|» marker|body|string|false|Marker to use for requesting the next page.|
|» order_by|body|[object]|false|A list of template fields and directions to sort the metadata query<br>results by.<br><br>The ordering `direction` must be the same for each item in the array.|
|» » direction|body|string|false|The direction to order by, either ascending or descending.<br><br>The `ordering` direction must be the same for each item in the<br>array.|
|» » field_key|body|string|false|The metadata template field to order by.<br><br>The `field_key` represents the `key` value of a field from the<br>metadata template being searched for.|
|» query|body|string|false|The query to perform. A query is a logical expression that is very similar<br>to a SQL `SELECT` statement. Values in the search query can be turned into<br>parameters specified in the `query_param` arguments list to prevent having<br>to manually insert search values into the query string.<br><br>For example, a value of `:amount` would represent the `amount` value in<br>`query_params` object.|
|» query_params|body|object|false|Set of arguments corresponding to the parameters specified in the<br>`query`. The type of each parameter used in the `query_params` must match<br>the type of the corresponding metadata template field.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|The value for the argument being used in the metadata search.<br><br>The type of this parameter must match the type of the corresponding<br>metadata template field.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » direction|ASC|
|» » direction|DESC|
|» » direction|asc|
|» » direction|desc|

This can mean the `query` is incorrect, as well as some cases<br>where the `from` value does not represent a valid template.<br>* `unexpected_json_type` - An argument from the `query` string is not<br>present in `query_param`. For example, `query` of `name = :name` requires<br>the `query_param` to include a value for the `name` argument, for example<br>`{ "name": "Box, Inc" }`.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
