The error response will include extra<br>details.<br><br>* `instance_not_found` - The template was not found. Please make sure<br>to use the full template scope including the enterprise ID, like<br>`enterprise_12345`.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

## Search for content

<a id="opIdget_search"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/search \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /search`

Searches for files, folders, web links, and shared files across the
users content or across the entire enterprise.

<h3 id="search-for-content-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|query|query|string|false|The string to search for. This query is matched against item names,<br>descriptions, text content of files, and various other fields of<br>the different item types.<br><br>This parameter supports a variety of operators to further refine<br>the results returns.<br><br>* `""` - by wrapping a query in double quotes only exact matches are<br>  returned by the API. Exact searches do not return search matches<br>  based on specific character sequences. Instead, they return<br>  matches based on phrases, that is, word sequences. For example:<br>  A search for `"Blue-Box"` may return search results including<br>  the sequence `"blue.box"`, `"Blue Box"`, and `"Blue-Box"`;<br>  any item containing the words `Blue` and `Box` consecutively, in<br>  the order specified.<br>* `AND` - returns items that contain both the search terms. For<br>  example, a search for `marketing AND BoxWorks` returns items<br>  that have both `marketing` and `BoxWorks` within its text in any order.<br>  It does not return a result that only has `BoxWorks` in its text.<br>* `OR` - returns items that contain either of the search terms. For<br>  example, a search for `marketing OR BoxWorks` returns a result that<br>  has either `marketing` or `BoxWorks` within its text. Using this<br>  operator is not necessary as we implicitly interpret multi-word<br>  queries as `OR` unless another supported boolean term is used.<br>* `NOT` - returns items that do not contain the search term provided.<br>  For example, a search for `marketing AND NOT BoxWorks` returns a result<br>  that has only `marketing` within its text. Results containing<br>  `BoxWorks` are omitted.<br><br>Please note that we do not support lower case (that is,<br>`and`, `or`, and `not`) or mixed case (that is, `And`, `Or`, and `Not`)<br>operators.<br><br>This field is required unless the `mdfilters` parameter is defined.|
|scope|query|string|false|Limits the search results to either the files that the user has<br>access to, or to files available to the entire enterprise.<br><br>The scope defaults to `user_content`, which limits the search<br>results to content that is available to the currently authenticated<br>user.<br><br>The `enterprise_content` can be requested by an admin through our<br>support channels. Once this scope has been enabled for a user, it<br>will allow that use to query for content across the entire<br>enterprise and not only the content that they have access to.|
|file_extensions|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to any files that match any of the provided<br>file extensions. This list is a comma-separated list of file extensions<br>without the dots.|
|created_at_range|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to any items created within<br>a given date range.<br><br>Date ranges are defined as comma separated RFC3339<br>timestamps.<br><br>If the the start date is omitted (`,2014-05-17T13:35:01-07:00`)<br>anything created before the end date will be returned.<br><br>If the end date is omitted (`2014-05-15T13:35:01-07:00,`) the<br>current date will be used as the end date instead.|
|updated_at_range|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to any items updated within<br>a given date range.<br><br>Date ranges are defined as comma separated RFC3339<br>timestamps.<br><br>If the start date is omitted (`,2014-05-17T13:35:01-07:00`)<br>anything updated before the end date will be returned.<br><br>If the end date is omitted (`2014-05-15T13:35:01-07:00,`) the<br>current date will be used as the end date instead.|
|size_range|query|[integer]|false|Limits the search results to any items with a size within<br>a given file size range. This applied to files and folders.<br><br>Size ranges are defined as comma separated list of a lower<br>and upper byte size limit (inclusive).<br><br>The upper and lower bound can be omitted to create open ranges.|
|owner_user_ids|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to any items that are owned<br>by the given list of owners, defined as a list of comma separated<br>user IDs.<br><br>Please note that the items still need to be owned or shared with<br>the currently authenticated user for them to show up in the search<br>results. If the user does not have access to any files owned by any of<br>the users an empty result set will be returned.<br><br>To search across an entire enterprise, we recommend using the<br>`enterprise_content` scope parameter which can be requested with our<br>support team.|
|recent_updater_user_ids|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to any items that have been updated<br>by the given list of users, defined as a list of comma separated<br>user IDs.<br><br>Please note that the items still need to be owned or shared with<br>the currently authenticated user for them to show up in the search<br>results. If the user does not have access to any files owned by any of<br>the users an empty result set will be returned.<br><br>This feature only searches back to the last 10 versions of an item.|
|ancestor_folder_ids|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to items within the given<br>list of folders, defined as a comma separated lists<br>of folder IDs.<br><br>Search results will also include items within any subfolders<br>of those ancestor folders.<br><br>Please note that the folders still need to be owned or shared with<br>the currently authenticated user. If the folder is not accessible by this<br>user, or it does not exist, a `HTTP 404` error code will be returned<br>instead.<br><br>To search across an entire enterprise, we recommend using the<br>`enterprise_content` scope parameter which can be requested with our<br>support team.|
|content_types|query|[string]|false|Limits the search results to any items that match the search query<br>for a specific part of the file, for example the file description.<br><br>Content types are defined as a comma separated lists<br>of Box recognized content types. The allowed content types are as follows.<br><br>* `name` - The name of the item, as defined by its `name` field.<br>* `description` - The description of the item, as defined by its<br>  `description` field.<br>* `file_content` - The actual content of the file.<br>* `comments` - The content of any of the comments on a file or<br>   folder.<br>* `tags` - Any tags that are applied to an item, as defined by its<br>   `tags` field.|
|type|query|string|false|Limits the search results to any items of this type. This<br>parameter only takes one value. By default the API returns<br>items that match any of these types.<br><br>* `file` - Limits the search results to files<br>* `folder` - Limits the search results to folders<br>* `web_link` - Limits the search results to web links, also known<br>   as bookmarks|
|trash_content|query|string|false|Determines if the search should look in the trash for items.<br><br>By default, this API only returns search results for items<br>not currently in the trash (`non_trashed_only`).<br><br>* `trashed_only` - Only searches for items currently in the trash<br>* `non_trashed_only` - Only searches for items currently not in<br>  the trash|
|mdfilters|query|[[MetadataFilter](#schemametadatafilter)]|false|Limits the search results to any items for which the metadata matches<br>the provided filter.<br><br>This parameter contains a list of 1 metadata template to filter<br>the search results by. This list can currently only<br>contain one entry, though this might be expanded in the future.<br><br>This parameter is required unless the `query` parameter is provided.|
|sort|query|string|false|Defines the order in which search results are returned. This API<br>defaults to returning items by relevance unless this parameter is<br>explicitly specified.<br><br>* `relevance` (default) returns the results sorted by relevance to the<br>query search term. The relevance is based on the occurrence of the search<br>term in the items name, description, content, and additional properties.<br>* `modified_at` returns the results ordered in descending order by date<br>at which the item was last modified.|
|direction|query|string|false|Defines the direction in which search results are ordered. This API<br>defaults to returning items in descending (`DESC`) order unless this<br>parameter is explicitly specified.<br><br>When results are sorted by `relevance` the ordering is locked to returning<br>items in descending order of relevance, and this parameter is ignored.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|Defines the maximum number of items to return as part of a page of<br>results.|
|include_recent_shared_links|query|boolean|false|Defines whether the search results should include any items<br>that the user recently accessed through a shared link.<br><br>Please note that when this parameter has been set to true,<br>the format of the response of this API changes to return<br>a list of [Search Results with<br>Shared Links](r://search_results_with_shared_links)|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Queries with offset parameter value<br>exceeding 10000 will be rejected<br>with a 400 response.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|scope|user_content|
|scope|enterprise_content|
|content_types|name|
|content_types|description|
|content_types|file_content|
|content_types|comments|
|content_types|tag|
|type|file|
|type|folder|
|type|web_link|
|trash_content|non_trashed_only|
|trash_content|trashed_only|
|sort|modified_at|
|sort|relevance|
|direction|DESC|
|direction|ASC|

<h3 id="search-for-content-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a collection of search results. If there are no matching<br>search results, the `entries` array will be empty.|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Returns an error when the request was not valid. This can have multiple<br>reasons and the `context_info` object will provide you with more details.<br><br>* `missing_parameter` - Please provide at least the `query` or `mdfilters`<br>  query parameter in a search.<br>* `invalid_parameter` - Any of the fields might not be in the right<br>  format. This could for example mean that one of the RFC3339 dates is<br>  incorrect, or a string is provided where an integer is expected.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|403|Forbidden|Returns an error when the user does not have the permission to make<br>this API call.<br><br>* The developer provided a `scope` of `enterprise_content` but did<br>  not request this scope to be enabled for the user through our<br>  support channels.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|404|Not Found|Returns an error when the user does not have access to an item<br>mentioned in the request.<br><br>* The developer provided a folder ID in `ancestor_folder_ids`<br>  that either does not exist or the user does not have access to.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<h3 id="search-for-content-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|[SearchResults](#schemasearchresults)|false|none|A list of files, folders and web links that matched the search query.|
|*oneOf*|[SearchResultsWithSharedLinks](#schemasearchresultswithsharedlinks)|false|none|A list of files, folders and web links that matched the search query,<br>including the additional information about any shared links through<br>which the item has been shared with the user.<br><br>This response format is only returned when the `include_recent_shared_links`<br>query parameter has been set to `true`.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

<h1 id="box-platform-api-shared-links-files">Shared links (Files)</h1>

## Add shared link to file

<a id="opIdput_files_id#add_shared_link"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/files/12345#add_shared_link?fields=shared_link' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "shared_link": {
      "access": "open",
      "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
      "permissions": {
        "can_download": true,
        "can_edit": true,
        "can_preview": true
      },
      "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /files/{file_id}#add_shared_link`

Adds a shared link to a file.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
    "permissions": {
      "can_download": true,
      "can_edit": true,
      "can_preview": true
    },
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-shared-link-to-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|fields|query|string|true|Explicitly request the `shared_link` fields<br>to be returned for this item.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» shared_link|body|object|false|The settings for the shared link to create on the file.<br>Use an empty object (`{}`) to use the default settings for shared<br>links.|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the file (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br><br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » permissions|body|object|false|none|
|» » » can_download|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for downloading of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.|
|» » » can_edit|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for editing of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.<br>This value can only be `true` is `can_download` is<br>also `true`.|
|» » » can_preview|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for previewing of files.<br>This value is always `true`. For shared links on folders<br>this also applies to any items in the folder.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts. The value must be greater than the<br>current date and time.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared<br>links.|

|412|Precondition Failed|Returns an error when the `If-Match` header does not match<br>the current `etag` value of the file. This indicates that the file<br>has changed since it was last requested.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Find file for shared link

<a id="opIdget_shared_items"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/shared_items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'boxapi: shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]'
```

`GET /shared_items`

Returns the file represented by a shared link.

A shared file can be represented by a shared link,
which can originate within the current enterprise or within another.

This endpoint allows an application to retrieve information about a
shared file when only given a shared link.

The `shared_link_permission_options` array field can be returned
by requesting it in the `fields` query parameter.

<h3 id="find-file-for-shared-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|if-none-match|header|string|false|Ensures an item is only returned if it has changed.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `304 Not Modified` if the item has not<br>changed since.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|boxapi|header|string|true|A header containing the shared link and optional password for the<br>shared link.<br><br>The format for this header is as follows.<br><br>`shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]`|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-shared-links-folders">Shared links (Folders)</h1>

## Add shared link to folder

<a id="opIdput_folders_id#add_shared_link"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/folders/12345#add_shared_link?fields=shared_link' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "shared_link": {
      "access": "open",
      "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
      "permissions": {
        "can_download": true,
        "can_edit": false,
        "can_preview": true
      },
      "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /folders/{folder_id}#add_shared_link`

Adds a shared link to a folder.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
    "permissions": {
      "can_download": true,
      "can_edit": false,
      "can_preview": true
    },
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="add-shared-link-to-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|fields|query|string|true|Explicitly request the `shared_link` fields<br>to be returned for this item.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» shared_link|body|object|false|The settings for the shared link to create on the folder.<br><br>Use an empty object (`{}`) to use the default settings for shared<br>links.|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the folder (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br><br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » permissions|body|object|false|none|
|» » » can_download|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for downloading of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.|
|» » » can_edit|body|boolean|false|This value can only be `false` for items<br>with a `type` of `folder`.|
|» » » can_preview|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for previewing of files.<br>This value is always `true`. For shared links on folders<br>this also applies to any items in the folder.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts. The value must be greater than the<br>current date and time.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared<br>links.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » access|open|
|» » access|company|
|» » access|collaborators|

  }'
```

`PUT /folders/{folder_id}#update_shared_link`

Updates a shared link on a folder.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
    "permissions": {
      "can_download": true,
      "can_edit": false,
      "can_preview": true
    },
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-shared-link-on-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|fields|query|string|true|Explicitly request the `shared_link` fields<br>to be returned for this item.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» shared_link|body|object|false|The settings for the shared link to update.|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the folder (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br><br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » permissions|body|object|false|none|
|» » » can_download|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for downloading of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.|
|» » » can_edit|body|boolean|false|This value can only be `false` for items<br>with a `type` of `folder`.|
|» » » can_preview|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for previewing of files.<br>This value is always `true`. For shared links on folders<br>this also applies to any items in the folder.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts. The value must be greater than the<br>current date and time.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared<br>links.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » access|open|
|» » access|company|
|» » access|collaborators|

## Find folder for shared link

<a id="opIdget_shared_items#folders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/shared_items#folders' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'boxapi: shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]'
```

`GET /shared_items#folders`

Return the folder represented by a shared link.

A shared folder can be represented by a shared link,
which can originate within the current enterprise or within another.

This endpoint allows an application to retrieve information about a
shared folder when only given a shared link.

<h3 id="find-folder-for-shared-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|if-none-match|header|string|false|Ensures an item is only returned if it has changed.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `304 Not Modified` if the item has not<br>changed since.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|boxapi|header|string|true|A header containing the shared link and optional password for the<br>shared link.<br><br>The format for this header is as follows.<br><br>`shared_link=[link]&shared_link_password=[password]`|

## Add shared link to web link

<a id="opIdput_web_links_id#add_shared_link"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/web_links/12345#add_shared_link?fields=shared_link' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

  -d '{

        "can_edit": false,
        "can_preview": true
      },
      "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /web_links/{web_link_id}#add_shared_link`

Adds a shared link to a web link.

## Update shared link on web link

<a id="opIdput_web_links_id#update_shared_link"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/web_links/12345#update_shared_link?fields=shared_link' \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "shared_link": {
      "access": "open",
      "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
      "permissions": {
        "can_download": true,
        "can_edit": true,
        "can_preview": true
      },
      "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /web_links/{web_link_id}#update_shared_link`

Updates a shared link on a web link.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
    "permissions": {
      "can_download": true,
      "can_edit": true,
      "can_preview": true
    },
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="update-shared-link-on-web-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|web_link_id|path|string|true|The ID of the web link.|
|fields|query|string|true|Explicitly request the `shared_link` fields<br>to be returned for this item.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» shared_link|body|object|false|The settings for the shared link to update.|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the folder (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br><br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » permissions|body|object|false|none|
|» » » can_download|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for downloading of files.<br>This can only be set when `access` is set to<br>`open` or `company`.|
|» » » can_edit|body|boolean|false|This value can only be `true` is `type` is `file`.|
|» » » can_preview|body|boolean|false|If the shared link allows for previewing of files.<br>This value is always `true`. For shared links on folders<br>this also applies to any items in the folder.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts. The value must be greater than the<br>current date and time.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared<br>links.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » access|open|
|» » access|company|
|» » access|collaborators|

> 200 Response

  "etag": "1",
  "id": "12345",
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "download_count": 0,
    "download_url": "https://app.box.com/shared/static/kwio6b4ovt1264rnfbyqo1.pdf",
    "effective_access": "open",
    "effective_permission": "can_download",
    "is_password_enabled": false,

<h1 id="box-platform-api-task-assignments">Task assignments</h1>

## Assign task

<a id="opIdpost_task_assignments"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/task_assignments \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "assign_to": {
      "id": "3242343",
      "login": "john@example.com"
    },
    "task": {
      "id": "11446498",
      "type": "task"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /task_assignments`

Assigns a task to a user.

A task can be assigned to more than one user by creating multiple
assignments.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "assign_to": {
    "id": "3242343",
    "login": "john@example.com"
  },
  "task": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "task"
  }
}
```

|» » id|body|string|false|The ID of the user to assign to the<br>task.<br><br>To specify a user by their email<br>address use the `login` parameter.|

## Update task assignment

<a id="opIdput_task_assignments_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/task_assignments/12345 \

  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "message": "Looks good to me",
    "resolution_state": "completed"
  }'

`PUT /task_assignments/{task_assignment_id}`

Updates a task assignment. This endpoint can be
used to update the state of a task assigned to a user.

> Body parameter

```json

  "message": "Looks good to me",
  "resolution_state": "completed"
}

|body|body|object|false|none|
|» message|body|string|false|An optional message by the assignee that can be added to the task.|
|» resolution_state|body|string|false|The state of the task assigned to the user.<br><br>* For a task with an `action` value of `complete` this can be<br>`incomplete` or `completed`.<br>* For a task with an `action` of `review` this can be<br>`incomplete`, `approved`, or `rejected`.|

## Create task

<a id="opIdpost_tasks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/tasks \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "action": "review",
    "completion_rule": "all_assignees",
    "due_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "item": {
      "id": "11446498",
      "type": "file"
    },
    "message": "Please review"
  }'
```

`POST /tasks`

Creates a single task on a file. This task is not assigned to any user and
will need to be assigned separately.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "action": "review",
  "completion_rule": "all_assignees",
  "due_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "item": {
    "id": "11446498",
    "type": "file"
  },
  "message": "Please review"
}
```

<h3 id="create-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» action|body|string|false|The action the task assignee will be prompted to do. Must be<br><br>* `review` defines an approval task that can be approved or<br>rejected<br>* `complete` defines a general task which can be completed|
|» completion_rule|body|string|false|Defines which assignees need to complete this task before the task<br>is considered completed.<br><br>* `all_assignees` (default) requires all assignees to review or<br>approve the the task in order for it to be considered completed.<br>* `any_assignee` accepts any one assignee to review or<br>approve the the task in order for it to be considered completed.|
|» due_at|body|string(date-time)|false|Defines when the task is due. Defaults to `null` if not<br>provided.|
|» item|body|object|true|The file to attach the task to.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the file|
|» » type|body|string|true|`file`|
|» message|body|string|false|An optional message to include with the task.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|review|
|» action|complete|
|» completion_rule|all_assignees|
|» completion_rule|any_assignee|
|» » type|file|

## Update task

<a id="opIdput_tasks_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/tasks/12345 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "action": "review",
    "completion_rule": "all_assignees",
    "due_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "message": "Please review"
  }'
```

`PUT /tasks/{task_id}`

Updates a task. This can be used to update a task's configuration, or to
update its completion state.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "action": "review",
  "completion_rule": "all_assignees",
  "due_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
  "message": "Please review"
}
```

<h3 id="update-task-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|task_id|path|string|true|The ID of the task.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» action|body|string|false|The action the task assignee will be prompted to do. Must be<br><br>* `review` defines an approval task that can be approved or<br>rejected<br>* `complete` defines a general task which can be completed|
|» completion_rule|body|string|false|Defines which assignees need to complete this task before the task<br>is considered completed.<br><br>* `all_assignees` (default) requires all assignees to review or<br>approve the the task in order for it to be considered completed.<br>* `any_assignee` accepts any one assignee to review or<br>approve the the task in order for it to be considered completed.|
|» due_at|body|string(date-time)|false|When the task is due at.|
|» message|body|string|false|The message included with the task.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» action|review|
|» action|complete|
|» completion_rule|all_assignees|
|» completion_rule|any_assignee|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-transfer-folders">Transfer folders</h1>

## Transfer owned folders

<a id="opIdput_users_id_folders_0"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/users/12345/folders/0 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "owned_by": {
      "id": "1232234"
    }
  }'
```

`PUT /users/{user_id}/folders/0`

Move all of the items (files, folders and workflows) owned by a user into
another user's account

Only the root folder (`0`) can be transferred.

Folders can only be moved across users by users with administrative
permissions.

All existing shared links and folder-level collaborations are transferred
during the operation. Please note that while collaborations at the individual
file-level are transferred during the operation, the collaborations are
deleted when the original user is deleted.

This call will be performed synchronously which might lead to a slow response
when the source user has a large number of items in all of its folders.

If the destination path has a metadata cascade policy attached to any of
the parent folders, a metadata cascade operation will be kicked off
asynchronously.

There is currently no way to check for when this operation is finished.

The destination folder's name will be in the format `{User}'s Files and
Folders`, where `{User}` is the display name of the user.

To make this API call your application will need to have the "Read and write
all files and folders stored in Box" scope enabled.

Please make sure the destination user has access to `Relay` or `Relay Lite`,
and has access to the files and folders involved in the workflows being
transferred.

Admins will receive an email when the operation is completed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "owned_by": {
    "id": "1232234"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="transfer-owned-folders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|notify|query|boolean|false|Determines if users should receive email notification<br>for the action performed.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» owned_by|body|object|true|The user who the folder will be transferred to|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of the user who the folder will be<br>transferred to|

## Get trashed file

<a id="opIdget_files_id_trash"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/files/12345/trash \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /files/{file_id}/trash`

Retrieves a file that has been moved to the trash.

Please note that only if the file itself has been moved to the
trash can it be retrieved with this API call. If instead one of
its parent folders was moved to the trash, only that folder
can be inspected using the
[`GET /folders/:id/trash`](e://get_folders_id_trash) API.

To list all items that have been moved to the trash, please
use the [`GET /folders/trash/items`](e://get-folders-trash-items/)
API.

<h3 id="get-trashed-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-trashed-folders">Trashed folders</h1>

## Restore folder

<a id="opIdpost_folders_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/folders/12345 \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Restored Photos",
    "parent": {
      "id": "123"
    }
  }'
```

`POST /folders/{folder_id}`

Restores a folder that has been moved to the trash.

An optional new parent ID can be provided to restore the folder to in case the
original folder has been deleted.

# Folder locking

During this operation, part of the file tree will be locked, mainly
the source folder and all of its descendants, as well as the destination
folder.

For the duration of the operation, no other move, copy, delete, or restore
operation can performed on any of the locked folders.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "name": "Restored Photos",
  "parent": {
    "id": "123"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="restore-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» name|body|string|false|An optional new name for the folder.|
|» parent|body|object|false|none|
|» » id|body|string|false|The ID of parent item|

## Get trashed folder

<a id="opIdget_folders_id_trash"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/folders/12345/trash \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /folders/{folder_id}/trash`

Retrieves a folder that has been moved to the trash.

Please note that only if the folder itself has been moved to the
trash can it be retrieved with this API call. If instead one of
its parent folders was moved to the trash, only that folder
can be inspected using the
[`GET /folders/:id/trash`](e://get_folders_id_trash) API.

To list all items that have been moved to the trash, please
use the [`GET /folders/trash/items`](e://get-folders-trash-items/)
API.

<h3 id="get-trashed-folder-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-trashed-items">Trashed items</h1>

## List trashed items

<a id="opIdget_folders_trash_items"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/folders/trash/items \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /folders/trash/items`

Retrieves the files and folders that have been moved
to the trash.

Any attribute in the full files or folders objects can be passed
in with the `fields` parameter to retrieve those specific
attributes that are not returned by default.

This endpoint defaults to use offset-based pagination, yet also supports
marker-based pagination using the `marker` parameter.

<h3 id="list-trashed-items-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Queries with offset parameter value<br>exceeding 10000 will be rejected<br>with a 400 response.|
|usemarker|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether to use marker-based pagination instead of<br>offset-based pagination. Only one pagination method can<br>be used at a time.<br><br>By setting this value to true, the API will return a `marker` field<br>that can be passed as a parameter to this endpoint to get the next<br>page of the response.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|direction|query|string|false|The direction to sort results in. This can be either in alphabetical ascending<br>(`ASC`) or descending (`DESC`) order.|
|sort|query|string|false|Defines the **second** attribute by which items<br>are sorted.<br><br>Items are always sorted by their `type` first, with<br>folders listed before files, and files listed<br>before web links.<br><br>This parameter is not supported when using marker-based pagination.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|direction|ASC|
|direction|DESC|
|sort|id|
|sort|name|
|sort|date|
|sort|size|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "limit": 1000,
  "offset": 2000,
  "order": [
    {
      "by": "type",
      "direction": "ASC"
    }
  ],
  "total_count": 5000,
  "entries": [
    {
      "etag": "1",
      "id": "12345",
      "type": "file",
      "file_version": {
        "id": "12345",
        "type": "file_version",
        "sha1": "134b65991ed521fcfe4724b7d814ab8ded5185dc"
      },
      "name": "Contract.pdf",
      "sequence_id": {},
      "sha1": "85136C79CBF9FE36BB9D05D0639C70C265C18D37"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong."
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",
  "message": "Method Not Allowed",
  "request_id": "abcdef123456",
  "status": 400,
  "type": "error"
}
```

> default Response

  "code": "item_name_invalid",
  "context_info": {
    "message": "Something went wrong."
  },
  "help_url": "https://developer.box.com/guides/api-calls/permissions-and-errors/common-errors/",

|400|Bad Request|Returns an error if some of the parameters are missing or<br>not valid.<br><br>* `invalid_parameter` can appear when the `sort`, `direction` or `offset`<br>parameter is provided when using marker based pagination, or when the<br>`marker` parameter is provided but `usemarker` is set to `false` or<br>`null`.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

`POST /web_links/{web_link_id}`

Restores a web link that has been moved to the trash.

An optional new parent ID can be provided to restore the  web link to in case
the original folder has been deleted.

> Body parameter

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-uploads">Uploads</h1>

## Upload file

<a id="opIdpost_files_content"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/files/content \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'attributes={"content_created_at":"2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00","content_modified_at":"2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00","name":"Photo.png","parent":{"id":"124132"}}' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /files/content`

Uploads a small file to Box. For file sizes over 50MB we recommend
using the Chunk Upload APIs.

# Request body order

The `attributes` part of the body must come **before** the
`file` part. Requests that do not follow this format when
uploading the file will receive a HTTP `400` error with a
`metadata_after_file_contents` error code.

> Body parameter

```yaml
attributes:
  content_created_at: "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00"
  content_modified_at: "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00"
  name: Photo.png
  parent:
    id: "124132"
file: string
```

<h3 id="upload-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|content-md5|header|string|false|An optional header containing the SHA1 hash of the file to<br>ensure that the file was not corrupted in transit.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» attributes|body|object|true|The additional attributes of the file being uploaded. Mainly the<br>name and the parent folder. These attributes are part of the multi<br>part request body and are in JSON format.<br><br><Message warning><br><br>  The `attributes` part of the body must come **before** the<br>  `file` part. Requests that do not follow this format when<br>  uploading the file will receive a HTTP `400` error with a<br>  `metadata_after_file_contents` error code.<br><br></Message>|
|» » content_created_at|body|string(date-time)|false|Defines the time the file was originally created at.<br><br>If not set, the upload time will be used.|
|» » content_modified_at|body|string(date-time)|false|Defines the time the file was last modified at.<br><br>If not set, the upload time will be used.|
|» » name|body|string|true|The name of the file|
|» » parent|body|object|true|The parent folder to upload the file to|
|» » » id|body|string|true|The id of the parent folder. Use<br>`0` for the user's root folder.|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The content of the file to upload to Box.<br><br><Message warning><br><br>  The `attributes` part of the body must come **before** the<br>  `file` part. Requests that do not follow this format when<br>  uploading the file will receive a HTTP `400` error with a<br>  `metadata_after_file_contents` error code.<br><br></Message>|

<h3 id="upload-file-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|Returns the new file object in a list.|[Files](#schemafiles)|
|400|Bad Request|Returns an error if some of the parameters are missing or<br>not valid.<br>* `bad_request` when a parameter is missing or incorrect.<br>* `item_name_too_long` when the folder name is too long.<br>* `item_name_invalid` when the folder name contains<br>  non-valid characters.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|409|Conflict|Returns an error if the file already exists,<br>or the account has run out of disk space.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
OAuth2Security
</aside>

## Upload file version

<a id="opIdpost_files_id_content"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/files/12345/content \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -F 'attributes={"content_modified_at":"2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00","name":"Photo 2.0.png"}' \
  -F 'file=@/path/to/file'
```

`POST /files/{file_id}/content`

Update a file's content. For file sizes over 50MB we recommend
using the Chunk Upload APIs.

# Request body order

The `attributes` part of the body must come **before** the
`file` part. Requests that do not follow this format when
uploading the file will receive a HTTP `400` error with a
`metadata_after_file_contents` error code.

> Body parameter

```yaml
attributes:
  content_modified_at: "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00"
  name: Photo 2.0.png
file: string
```

<h3 id="upload-file-version-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|file_id|path|string|true|The unique identifier that represents a file.<br><br>The ID for any file can be determined<br>by visiting a file in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/files/123`<br>the `file_id` is `123`.|
|if-match|header|string|false|Ensures this item hasn't recently changed before<br>making changes.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `412 Precondition Failed` if it<br>has changed since.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|content-md5|header|string|false|An optional header containing the SHA1 hash of the file to<br>ensure that the file was not corrupted in transit.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» attributes|body|object|true|The additional attributes of the file being uploaded. Mainly the<br>name and the parent folder. These attributes are part of the multi<br>part request body and are in JSON format.<br><br><Message warning><br><br>  The `attributes` part of the body must come **before** the<br>  `file` part. Requests that do not follow this format when<br>  uploading the file will receive a HTTP `400` error with a<br>  `metadata_after_file_contents` error code.<br><br></Message>|
|» » content_modified_at|body|string(date-time)|false|Defines the time the file was last modified at.<br><br>If not set, the upload time will be used.|
|» » name|body|string|true|An optional new name for the file. If specified, the file<br>will be renamed when the new version is uploaded.|
|» file|body|string(binary)|true|The content of the file to upload to Box.<br><br><Message warning><br><br>  The `attributes` part of the body must come **before** the<br>  `file` part. Requests that do not follow this format when<br>  uploading the file will receive a HTTP `400` error with a<br>  `metadata_after_file_contents` error code.<br><br></Message>|

|404|Not Found|Returns an error if the parent folder could not be found, or<br>the authenticated user does not have access to it.<br><br>* `invalid_parameter`: The `folder_id` value represents a<br>  folder that the user does not have access to, or does not<br>  exist.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|409|Conflict|Returns an error if the file already exists,<br>or the account has run out of disk space.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|
|default|Default|An unexpected client error.|[ClientError](#schemaclienterror)|

## Upload part of file

<a id="opIdput_files_upload_sessions_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/files/upload_sessions/D5E3F7A \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/octet-stream' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'digest: sha=fpRyg5eVQletdZqEKaFlqwBXJzM=' \
  -H 'content-range: bytes 8388608-16777215/445856194' \
  --data-binary '@/path/to/file'
```

`PUT /files/upload_sessions/{upload_session_id}`

Updates a chunk of an upload session for a file.

<h3 id="upload-part-of-file-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|upload_session_id|path|string|true|The ID of the upload session.|
|digest|header|string|true|The [RFC3230][1] message digest of the chunk uploaded.<br><br>Only SHA1 is supported. The SHA1 digest must be base64<br>encoded. The format of this header is as<br>`sha=BASE64_ENCODED_DIGEST`.<br><br>To get the value for the `SHA` digest, use the<br>openSSL command to encode the file part:<br>`openssl sha1 -binary <FILE_PART_NAME> \| base64`<br><br>[1]: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3230|
|content-range|header|string|true|The byte range of the chunk.<br><br>Must not overlap with the range of a part already<br>uploaded this session. Each part’s size must be<br>exactly equal in size to the part size specified<br>in the upload session that you created.<br>One exception is the last part of the file, as this can be smaller.<br><br>When providing the value for `content-range`, remember that:<br><br>* The lower bound of each part's byte range<br>  must be a multiple of the part size.<br>* The higher bound must be a multiple of the part size - 1.|
|body|body|string(binary)|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "part": {
    "offset": 16777216,
    "part_id": "6F2D3486",
    "size": 3222784,
    "sha1": "134b65991ed521fcfe4724b7d814ab8ded5185dc"
  }
}
```

> 409 Response

  "request_id": "abcdef123456",

}

## Commit upload session

<a id="opIdpost_files_upload_sessions_id_commit"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/files/upload_sessions/D5E3F7A/commit \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -H 'digest: sha=fpRyg5eVQletdZqEKaFlqwBXJzM=' \
  -d '{
    "parts": [
      {
        "offset": 16777216,
        "part_id": "6F2D3486",
        "size": 3222784,
        "sha1": "134b65991ed521fcfe4724b7d814ab8ded5185dc"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /files/upload_sessions/{upload_session_id}/commit`

Close an upload session and create a file from the
uploaded chunks.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "parts": [
    {
      "offset": 16777216,
      "part_id": "6F2D3486",
      "size": 3222784,
      "sha1": "134b65991ed521fcfe4724b7d814ab8ded5185dc"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="commit-upload-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|upload_session_id|path|string|true|The ID of the upload session.|
|digest|header|string|true|The [RFC3230][1] message digest of the whole file.<br><br>Only SHA1 is supported. The SHA1 digest must be Base64<br>encoded. The format of this header is as<br>`sha=BASE64_ENCODED_DIGEST`.<br><br>[1]: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3230|
|if-match|header|string|false|Ensures this item hasn't recently changed before<br>making changes.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `412 Precondition Failed` if it<br>has changed since.|
|if-none-match|header|string|false|Ensures an item is only returned if it has changed.<br><br>Pass in the item's last observed `etag` value<br>into this header and the endpoint will fail<br>with a `304 Not Modified` if the item has not<br>changed since.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» parts|body|[[UploadPart](#schemauploadpart)]|true|The list details for the uploaded parts|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-users">Users</h1>

## List enterprise users

<a id="opIdget_users"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/users \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /users`

Returns a list of all users for the Enterprise along with their `user_id`,
`public_name`, and `login`.

The application and the authenticated user need to
have the permission to look up users in the entire
enterprise.

<h3 id="list-enterprise-users-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|filter_term|query|string|false|Limits the results to only users who's `name` or<br>`login` start with the search term.<br><br>For externally managed users, the search term needs<br>to completely match the in order to find the user, and<br>it will only return one user at a time.|
|user_type|query|string|false|Limits the results to the kind of user specified.<br><br>* `all` returns every kind of user for whom the<br>  `login` or `name` partially matches the<br>  `filter_term`. It will only return an external user<br>  if the login matches the `filter_term` completely,<br>  and in that case it will only return that user.<br>* `managed` returns all managed and app users for whom<br>  the `login` or `name` partially matches the<br>  `filter_term`.<br>* `external` returns all external users for whom the<br>  `login` matches the `filter_term` exactly.|
|external_app_user_id|query|string|false|Limits the results to app users with the given<br>`external_app_user_id` value.<br><br>When creating an app user, an<br>`external_app_user_id` value can be set. This value can<br>then be used in this endpoint to find any users that<br>match that `external_app_user_id` value.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|
|offset|query|integer(int64)|false|The offset of the item at which to begin the response.<br><br>Queries with offset parameter value<br>exceeding 10000 will be rejected<br>with a 400 response.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|usemarker|query|boolean|false|Specifies whether to use marker-based pagination instead of<br>offset-based pagination. Only one pagination method can<br>be used at a time.<br><br>By setting this value to true, the API will return a `marker` field<br>that can be passed as a parameter to this endpoint to get the next<br>page of the response.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|user_type|all|
|user_type|managed|
|user_type|external|

      "by": "type",

## Get current user

<a id="opIdget_users_me"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/users/me \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /users/me`

Retrieves information about the user who is currently authenticated.

In the case of a client-side authenticated OAuth 2.0 application
this will be the user who authorized the app.

In the case of a JWT, server-side authenticated application
this will be the service account that belongs to the application
by default.

Use the `As-User` header to change who this API call is made on behalf of.

## Create jobs to terminate users session

<a id="opIdpost_users_terminate_sessions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/users/terminate_sessions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{

      "123456",
      "456789"
    ],
    "user_logins": [
      "user@sample.com",
      "user2@sample.com"
    ]
  }'

`POST /users/terminate_sessions`

Validates the roles and permissions of the user,
and creates asynchronous jobs
to terminate the user's sessions.
Returns the status for the POST request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "user_ids": [
    "123456",
    "456789"
  ],
  "user_logins": [
    "user@sample.com",
    "user2@sample.com"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="create-jobs-to-terminate-users-session-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» user_ids|body|[string]|true|A list of user IDs|
|» user_logins|body|[string]|true|A list of user logins|

## Get user

<a id="opIdget_users_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/users/12345 \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /users/{user_id}`

Retrieves information about a user in the enterprise.

The application and the authenticated user need to
have the permission to look up users in the entire
enterprise.

This endpoint also returns a limited set of information
for external users who are collaborated on content
owned by the enterprise for authenticated users with the
right scopes. In this case, disallowed fields will return
null instead.

|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user.|
|fields|query|[string]|false|A comma-separated list of attributes to include in the<br>response. This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|

  "address": "900 Jefferson Ave, Redwood City, CA 94063",
  "avatar_url": "https://www.box.com/api/avatar/large/181216415",

  "job_title": "CEO",

## Update user

<a id="opIdput_users_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/users/12345 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "address": "900 Jefferson Ave, Redwood City, CA 94063",
    "can_see_managed_users": true,
    "enterprise": null,
    "external_app_user_id": "my-user-1234",
    "is_exempt_from_device_limits": true,
    "is_exempt_from_login_verification": true,
    "is_external_collab_restricted": true,
    "is_password_reset_required": true,
    "is_sync_enabled": true,
    "job_title": "CEO",
    "language": "en",
    "login": "somename@box.com",
    "name": "Aaron Levie",
    "notification_email": {
      "email": "notifications@example.com"
    },
    "notify": true,
    "phone": "6509241374",
    "role": "user",
    "space_amount": 11345156112,
    "status": "active",
    "timezone": "Africa/Bujumbura",
    "tracking_codes": [
      {
        "name": "department",
        "type": "tracking_code",
        "value": "Sales"
      }
    ]
  }'
```

`PUT /users/{user_id}`

Updates a managed or app user in an enterprise. This endpoint
is only available to users and applications with the right
admin permissions.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address": "900 Jefferson Ave, Redwood City, CA 94063",
  "can_see_managed_users": true,
  "enterprise": null,

  "role": "user",
  "space_amount": 11345156112,
  "status": "active",
  "timezone": "Africa/Bujumbura",

    {
      "name": "department",
      "type": "tracking_code",
      "value": "Sales"
    }
  ]
}

This can be used to request fields that are<br>not normally returned in a standard response.<br><br>Be aware that specifying this parameter will have the<br>effect that none of the standard fields are returned in<br>the response unless explicitly specified, instead only<br>fields for the mini representation are returned, additional<br>to the fields requested.|

## Delete user

<a id="opIddelete_users_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/users/12345 \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`DELETE /users/{user_id}`

Deletes a user. By default this will fail if the user
still owns any content. Move their owned content first
before proceeding, or use the `force` field to delete
the user and their files.

<h3 id="delete-user-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|user_id|path|string|true|The ID of the user.|
|notify|query|boolean|false|Whether the user will receive email notification of<br>the deletion|

<h1 id="box-platform-api-web-links">Web links</h1>

## Create web link

<a id="opIdpost_web_links"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/web_links \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Cloud Content Management",
    "name": "Box Website",
    "parent": {
      "id": "0"
    },
    "shared_link": {
      "access": "open",
      "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
      "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
    },
    "url": "https://box.com"
  }'
```

`POST /web_links`

Creates a web link object within a folder.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Cloud Content Management",
  "name": "Box Website",
  "parent": {
    "id": "0"
  },
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
  },
  "url": "https://box.com"
}
```

<h3 id="create-web-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|Description of the web link.|
|» name|body|string|false|Name of the web link. Defaults to the URL if not set.|
|» parent|body|object|true|The parent folder to create the web link within.|
|» » id|body|string|true|The ID of parent folder|
|» shared_link|body|object|false|The settings for the shared link to update.|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the folder (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br><br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts. The value must be greater than the<br>current date and time.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared<br>links.|
|» url|body|string|true|The URL that this web link links to. Must start with<br>`"http://"` or `"https://"`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » access|open|
|» » access|company|
|» » access|collaborators|

## Update web link

<a id="opIdput_web_links_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/web_links/12345 \
  -X PUT \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Cloud Content Management",
    "name": "Box Website",
    "parent": {
      "id": "123"
    },
    "shared_link": {
      "access": "open",
      "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
      "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
      "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
    },
    "url": "https://box.com"
  }'
```

`PUT /web_links/{web_link_id}`

Updates a web link object.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Cloud Content Management",
  "name": "Box Website",
  "parent": {
    "id": "123"
  },
  "shared_link": {
    "access": "open",
    "password": "do-not-use-this-password",
    "unshared_at": "2012-12-12T10:53:43-08:00",
    "vanity_name": "my-shared-link"
  },
  "url": "https://box.com"
}
```

<h3 id="update-web-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|web_link_id|path|string|true|The ID of the web link.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» description|body|string|false|A new description of the web link.|
|» name|body|string|false|A new name for the web link. Defaults to the URL if not set.|
|» parent|body|object|false|none|
|» » id|body|string|false|The ID of parent item|
|» shared_link|body|object|false|The settings for the shared link to update.|
|» » access|body|string|false|The level of access for the shared link. This can be<br>restricted to anyone with the link (`open`), only people<br>within the company (`company`) and only those who<br>have been invited to the folder (`collaborators`).<br><br>If not set, this field defaults to the access level specified<br>by the enterprise admin. To create a shared link with this<br>default setting pass the `shared_link` object with<br>no `access` field, for example `{ "shared_link": {} }`.<br><br>The `company` access level is only available to paid<br>accounts.|
|» » password|body|string|false|The password required to access the shared link. Set the<br>password to `null` to remove it.<br><br>A password can only be set when `access` is set to `open`.|
|» » unshared_at|body|string(date-time)|false|The timestamp at which this shared link will<br>expire. This field can only be set by<br>users with paid accounts. The value must be greater than the<br>current date and time.|
|» » vanity_name|body|string|false|Defines a custom vanity name to use in the shared link URL,<br>for example `https://app.box.com/v/my-shared-link`.<br><br>Custom URLs should not be used when sharing sensitive content<br>as vanity URLs are a lot easier to guess than regular shared<br>links.|
|» url|body|string|false|The new URL that the web link links to. Must start with<br>`"http://"` or `"https://"`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » access|open|
|» » access|company|
|» » access|collaborators|

## List all webhooks

<a id="opIdget_webhooks"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/webhooks \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /webhooks`

Returns all defined webhooks for the requesting application.

This API only returns webhooks that are applied to files or folders that are
owned by the authenticated user. This means that an admin can not see webhooks
created by a service account unless the admin has access to those folders, and
vice versa.

<h3 id="list-all-webhooks-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "limit": 1000,
  "next_marker": 3000,
  "prev_marker": 1000,
  "entries": [
    {
      "id": "11446498",
      "target": {

        "type": "file"
      },

}

<h1 id="box-platform-api-workflows">Workflows</h1>

## List workflows

<a id="opIdget_workflows"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl 'https://example.com/workflows?folder_id=12345' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}"
```

`GET /workflows`

Returns list of workflows that act on a given `folder ID`, and
have a flow with a trigger type of `WORKFLOW_MANUAL_START`.

You application must be authorized to use the `Manage Box Relay` application
scope within the developer console in to use this endpoint.

<h3 id="list-workflows-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|folder_id|query|string|true|The unique identifier that represent a folder.<br><br>The ID for any folder can be determined<br>by visiting this folder in the web application<br>and copying the ID from the URL. For example,<br>for the URL `https://*.app.box.com/folder/123`<br>the `folder_id` is `123`.<br><br>The root folder of a Box account is<br>always represented by the ID `0`.|
|trigger_type|query|string|false|Type of trigger to search for.|
|limit|query|integer(int64)|false|The maximum number of items to return per page.|
|marker|query|string|false|Defines the position marker at which to begin returning results. This is<br>used when paginating using marker-based pagination.<br><br>This requires `usemarker` to be set to `true`.|

## Starts workflow based on request body

<a id="opIdpost_workflows_id_start"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://example.com/workflows/12345/start \
  -X POST \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "files": [
      {
        "id": "12345678",
        "type": "file"
      }
    ],

      "type": "flow"
    },
    "folder": {
      "id": "87654321",
      "type": "folder"
    },
